articles.title: Cowboys release QB Joe Milton, keep Sam Howell to backup Dak Prescott this season
articles.summary: Joe Milton spent last season as a backup in Dallas, and appeared in four games.
articles.body:
The Cowboys released the backup quarterback on Monday, ending his short tenure with the franchise. In a corresponding move, running back Emari Demercado was claimed by the Cowboys off waivers from Kansas City.

The New England Patriots selected Milton in the sixth round of the 2024 NFL Draft out of Tennessee. He spent his rookie season there, but only appeared in one game, and then landed in Dallas the following offseason.

In his one year backing up Dak Prescott with the Cowboys, Milton appeared in four games. He threw for 183 yards and a touchdown, with two interceptions, while completing 15 of his 24 attempts.

The Cowboys kept Milton and Howell on their 53-man roster on Sunday, along with Prescott. With Milton now gone, Howell will presumably be the backup for the Cowboys to start the season. The former North Carolina quarterback spent last season with the Seattle Seahawks, but was most recently a starter during the 2023 campaign with the Washington Commanders.

Prescott threw for 4,552 yards with 30 touchdowns and 10 interceptions last season, his 10th with the Cowboys. They went 7-9-1 and missed the playoffs for a second straight campaign.

The Cowboys will open the season against the New York Giants on Sept. 13.

articles.title: "Do something with your life": Patrick and Brittany Mahomes faced intense social media scrutiny as several controversies surrounded their family
articles.summary: NFL News: The weeks after Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs won Super Bowl LVII were supposed to be all about celebration. Instead, his family found it.
articles.body: The weeks after Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs won Super Bowl LVII were supposed to be all about celebration. Instead, his family found itself at the centre of several online controversies. From criticism aimed at Jackson Mahomes to backlash over a luxury gift for Patrick and Brittany's daughter, the attention quickly moved beyond the football field. Looking back now, these were stories from March 2023, not recent developments.Patrick Mahomes family faced social media scrutinyMuch of the attention focused on Jackson Mahomes, Patrick's younger brother and a prominent social media personality. During the Chiefs' Super Bowl celebrations, Jackson appeared briefly behind Patrick during a post-game interview and was criticised online for dancing in the background. He later apologised and moved away from the camera.The criticism continued during Kansas City's victory parade on February 15, 2023. Jackson shared footage of himself on stage with Patrick, writing, "Patrick and I just vibing at the parade!"The response was mixed. Some social media users felt Jackson was taking too much attention during a celebration centred on the team. Others criticised him more broadly, including comments such as, "Bro thinks he's on the team."Jackson also faced criticism after posting a photograph with his mother. Some commenters told him to "Get a job", despite his established career as a social media influencer. Another person wrote: "Do something with your life."Another viral moment involved Patrick Mahomes and a replica Vince Lombardi Trophy. A video appeared to show the quarterback handing the trophy to fans during the parade. The clip sparked criticism until it became clear that the object was a detailed replica made by a Chiefs fan and had been given to Mahomes.Tom Brady defended the celebration, saying: "Looks like appropriate parade behavior to me @PatrickMahomes."Brittany Mahomes backlash added to family dramaBrittany Mahomes also became a target of online criticism during the same period. Her celebrations following Patrick's victories had already attracted attention, and podcast host Joe Rogan later made a controversial comment about how people might treat her if she and Patrick divorced.Brittany responded sharply, writing: "Something about grown men talking s*** about someone's wife is real weird..."She followed it with another post that read: "Actually grown ass men hating on women in general is pathetic," which many interpreted as a further response to the discussion.Patrick and Brittany also faced criticism after sharing their daughter Sterling Skye's second birthday celebrations. The couple reportedly gifted her a Chanel purse valued at around $4,800. Some social media users questioned the decision, arguing that a luxury handbag was unnecessary for a two-year-old.Even Patrick's fashion choices became part of the conversation. He unveiled an Adidas sneaker colourway called "Family Time" for Sterling's birthday, but the design received mixed reactions online.Meanwhile, photographs of Patrick and Brittany at an NBA game prompted another wave of speculation, with some viewers reading too much into Patrick's expression.The most serious development involved allegations against Jackson concerning an incident at a Kansas City-area restaurant. A restaurant owner accused him of forcibly kissing her, while his lawyer denied the allegations and argued that the interactions needed to be viewed in their "proper context."These controversies belong firmly to 2023, when the Mahomes family was facing intense attention following the Super Bowl. They should not be presented as current events. What the period showed, however, was how quickly a championship celebration could turn into a wider social media storm for one of the NFL's most visible families.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Travis Kelce warned to ‘be careful’ as his post-NFL Hollywood plans leave the internet deeply divided
articles.summary: NFL News: Travis Kelce had already started looking beyond the football field in 2024, as the Kansas City Chiefs star spoke openly about his desire to explore Ho.
articles.body: Travis Kelce had already started looking beyond the football field in 2024, as the Kansas City Chiefs star spoke openly about his desire to explore Hollywood once his NFL career eventually ends. In an interview that year, Kelce admitted he was testing the waters in entertainment while still treating football as his priority. His comments drew plenty of attention online, with fans split over whether the tight end could make a successful transition to show business.Travis Kelce reveals plans to explore entertainment after the NFLThe remarks came during a 2024 interview with The Hollywood Reporter, when Kelce was spending time in Los Angeles and getting more familiar with the entertainment industry. At the time, the NFL star was still firmly focused on football, but he was also making an effort to understand what life beyond the sport might look like."It still is, and I'm out here in LA trying to get more comfortable in the entertainment world before we start back up with this football thing, knowing that that's my main focus in my life, and it'll always be that until I'm done playing," Kelce revealed.Kelce also made it clear that he was not treating acting as a simple extension of his celebrity status. He acknowledged that scripted entertainment was a new space for him and said he wanted to develop his own creative instincts rather than rush into projects."But I'm definitely still dabbling in the scripted world, the entertainment world and we'll see where that road takes me. I'm extremely excited, but at the same time, I know I'm a bit of an amateur in that world, so I definitely got to get comfortable and, I don't know, put my own creativity on it."His comments suggested a gradual approach. Rather than announcing a specific acting career, Kelce appeared interested in learning how the industry worked and finding opportunities that suited his personality.Travis Kelce's Hollywood ambitions spark mixed reactionsKelce was not exactly a stranger to entertainment by 2024. His 2023 appearance on Saturday Night Live gave viewers a chance to see his comedic side, while television commercials had already made him a familiar face outside the NFL.He had also expanded his profile through New Heights, the podcast he co-hosts with his brother Jason Kelce. The show had become an important part of his growing media presence and showed that his appeal could extend beyond game-day performances.Still, his Hollywood plans divided internet users. Some welcomed the possibility of seeing Kelce take on more entertainment projects, while others questioned whether success on a football field and popularity on television would translate into scripted acting.Social media reactions ranged from enthusiastic support to blunt skepticism. One Facebook user wrote, "Love him," while another offered a warning: "Oh boy Travis. Be careful."The debate was understandable. Kelce had already built a major public profile, but acting would require a different set of skills. His willingness to describe himself as an amateur also showed that he understood the difference.Since the original story was published in April 2024, Kelce's comments should be viewed as an account of his ambitions at that time, rather than a new 2026 announcement. What made the story notable was his early interest in building an entertainment career before eventually stepping away from professional football.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders welcome Savanna Dastrup after heartbreaking rejection nearly ended her dream
articles.summary: NFL News: For Savanna Dastrup, becoming a Dallas Cowboys cheerleader was never a passing childhood wish. She first fell in love with the team at 14 after watchi.
articles.body: For Savanna Dastrup, becoming a Dallas Cowboys cheerleader was never a passing childhood wish. She first fell in love with the team at 14 after watching Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders: Making the Team with her mother. One failed audition could have ended that dream, but the Orem High School graduate returned stronger, earned her place and is now preparing to step onto the field in Dallas.Savanna Dastrup turns Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders rejection into motivationDastrup knows better than most that making the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders requires more than talent. It demands discipline, resilience and the willingness to keep showing up when the outcome does not go your way.She auditioned for the team in 2025 and made it through training camp. Then came the setback she had feared. She was cut just one week before the final team was announced.The experience hurt, but it also gave her a reason to push harder.“I actually auditioned last year, made it through training camp and got cut, like, the week before the team was made,” Dastrup said. “It was super hard, super devastating. But it really motivated me to come back and work harder. And it meant that much more.”Instead of treating the rejection as the end of her journey, Dastrup decided to use it as fuel.“I wasn’t going to stop either,” Dastrup said. “If it wasn’t this year, I was going to audition again.”That determination eventually paid off. She made the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders this year and is now preparing for her first appearance in front of Cowboys fans.The achievement still feels surreal to her.“I can’t even believe it still,” Dastrup said. “I’m so used to coming and being like, ‘Am I going to get cut tonight?’ I think I still am trying to get out of that mindset. Like, Savanna, you made it.”Her journey began years earlier, when her mother introduced her to the popular reality series following the cheerleaders' auditions and training.“My mom was like, ‘You should watch Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders: Making the Team with me,’” Dastrup said. “So I watched it and I was like, ‘That’s what I want to do.’ From there, I was like, ‘Please, we have to go to a Cowboys game.’”That early fascination eventually became a serious goal.Dallas Cowboys cheerleader Savanna Dastrup credits family for her successWhile determination brought Dastrup back after rejection, she says her family gave her the foundation to keep pursuing the dream.Her father taught her the value of putting in extra work, a lesson that became especially important after her first audition ended in disappointment.“You fight and earn for your spot every single day,” she said. “My dad always told me to be the first at the studio, the last to leave - put in the extra work - and what’s meant to be will be.”Her Utah roots have also remained an important part of her journey.“Utah is definitely my rock,” she said. “I have the best supportive family, and I couldn’t be more grateful. And I think support was the biggest thing.”Now, that support system is preparing to make the trip to Texas to see Dastrup live out the dream she has carried since she was a teenager.“I don’t think my parents will miss a game,” Dastrup said. “Family, friends, everyoneI’m like, ‘Come on, everybody come to Texas.’”Even before her official debut, she can already feel the excitement building. Hearing “Thunderstruck” during practice gives her butterflies, and she expects the emotion to be even stronger when the music plays inside the stadium.“I would not be surprised if I had tears running down my face of happiness and joy the first time I do it,” she said.But perhaps the most meaningful part of Dastrup's story is what she hopes other young women take from it.“I hope that girls that get rejected or don’t make the team they want realize there is a bigger picture,” she said. “And just, yeah, don’t give up.”For Dastrup, those words are not simply advice. She has lived them. Her first rejection did not erase the dream. It made the moment she finally earned her Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders spot even more meaningful.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: First-time voters can apply to be on SIR list by September 30 in Maharashtra
articles.summary: MUMBAI: The draft voter li­st of Maharashtra’s special int­e­nsive revision, pu­b­lished on Monday, has 2 cr­o­re fewer voters than the previous elect.
articles.body: MUMBAI: The draft voter li­st of Maharashtra’s special int­e­nsive revision, pu­b­lished on Monday, has 2 cr­o­re fewer voters than the previous electoral roll. Mumbai is down by 36 lakh voters — a 35% fall.The electoral roll used ti­ll June had 9.8 crore voters, while the draft SIR roll has 7.7 crore voters, which is 21.1% lower. However, in real terms there are 1.9 crore fewer voters in the state on the draft list since 17 lakh voters were removed from one constituency owing to duplicati­on, but ha­ve been retained in the other. “The 17 lakh duplicate voters cannot be considered as excluded,” state chi­ef electoral officer S Chockalingam said.The reduction in voters is because their enumerati­on forms were not collected owing to them being reported as absent, shifted their residen­ce, dead or duplicate.Around 1.5cr of the 2cr vo­ters whose names have be­en excluded will have the opportunity to apply to be on the SIR list until Sept 30.This is the phase of filing claims and objections to the draft roll. First-time voters who turned 18 before Oct 1 can also apply to be on the SIR voter list during this one-month period till Sept.“Around 34 lakh voters were reported dead, while 17 lakh were related to duplicate registrations. Hence, around 1.5 crore of the 2 crore voters whose names have been excluded because they were absent or had shifted residence have the opportunity to apply to be on the electoral roll,” said Chockalingam.Citizens can check their names on the draft roll on the ECI portal and website of the state’s chief electoral officer as well as the website of the district election officers. The draft rolls are also available with recognised political parties at the district level.If citizens have been excluded from the list after they filled out the enumeration form and even if they have missed filling the enumeration form, they can fill out Form 6 to be included on the SIR voter list. They can also fill out Form 7 for deletion from the list and Form 8 for corrections in name, address, gender and so on.These forms can be filled out online on the above sites. Also, citizens can approach electoral registration officers in their assembly constituency — their addresses are on the website of the state’s chief electoral officer. Citizens can also approach booth level officers or block level agents appointed by political parties.Of the total 7.7 crore voters in the SIR draft list in the state, 3.9 crore are male and 3.7 crore female. Of the 2 crore voters who have not been included in the draft roll owing to uncollected forms, the highest numbers are from urban areas as a result of internal shifting and migration. articles.title: NFL Catchup: Cowboys Release Milton, Tunsil Goes on IR And Nabers Injury Update
articles.summary: Following initial 53-man roster cutdowns, NFL teams continued adjusting their active rosters through waiver claims, injury designations and more Monday.
articles.body: Following initial 53-man roster cutdowns, NFL teams continued adjusting their active rosters through waiver claims, injury designations and more Monday. The Dallas Cowboys made a surprise roster move in their quarterback room by waiving Joe Milton, leaving Sam Howell as the backup to Dak Prescott despite Milton's preseason performances. Meanwhile, the Washington Commanders placed left tackle Laremy Tunsil on injured reserve Monday. More NFC East news dropped as New York Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers stayed noncommittal about his Week 1 availability. And the Los Angeles Chargers made headlines by reuniting the Herbert brothers. Here is the latest from around the league on Monday: Cowboys Waive Backup QB Joe Milton With Week 1 right around the corner, the Dallas Cowboys made a surprising roster move on Monday morning. The Cowboys are waiving quarterback Joe Milton to make room for running back Emari Demercado, according to ESPN. The decision clears the path for Sam Howell to serve as Dak Prescott's backup quarterback to start the season. Milton was drafted in the sixth round of the 2024 NFL Draft by the New England Patriots out of Tennessee. Milton spent six years in college playing for both Michigan and Tennessee, but only started one full season during his redshirt senior year. With the Volunteers, Milton completed 64.5% of his passes for 2,813 yards with 20 touchdowns and five interceptions. Now with Milton’s NFL future up in the air, it will be worth keeping an eye on whether another team claims him off waivers. A player with his physical tools might not stay a free agent long and could find his way into a quarterback competition sooner rather than later. Commanders Place Laremy Tunsil On IR, Could Return This Season The Washington Commanders took a major roster hit on Monday afternoon. They’re placing five-time Pro Bowl offensive tackle Laremy Tunsil and defensive lineman Jer’Zhan Newton on injured reserve, according to ESPN. Both players could return later this season, but Tunsil faces a long recovery after tearing his triceps early in training camp. Newton faces a similar uphill battle after suffering a torn pectoral muscle during a preseason game against the Miami Dolphins. Tunsil played in 14 games last season for the Commanders after an offseason trade with the Houston Texans that brought in a true pass protector for quarterback Jayden Daniels. For a team repeatedly plagued by injuries, this season doesn’t appear to be any different. Missing Tunsil and Newton for most or even all of the 2026 season puts head coach Dan Quinn in a tough spot in a crowded and competitive NFC East. The Commanders are set to kick off their season on the road in Week 1 against the Philadelphia Eagles. Malik Nabers Noncommittal On Week 1 Availability New York Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers progressed from individual drills to full-contact team sessions at practice on Monday, shedding his no-contact jersey. However, with New York set to open its regular season against the Dallas Cowboys on Sept. 13, the wideout remains uncertain if he will be cleared in time as he recovers from a torn ACL in his right knee. "My mind is focused on playing the regular season: playing whenever that is," Nabers said after practice Monday. "There’s still some things that you still have to check off the box for you to participate. I’m still going through that, still listening to the trainers, still listening to doctors and sharing everything with them." Nabers added that he feels "real good" physically, but emphasized that final clearance remains a process between himself, doctors, and the coaching staff. "That’ll be a decision that will be made when that time comes," Nabers said regarding Week 1. "There’s certain things that, as a football player, you’ve got to mentally prepare (for) before you go into a game... I want to be able to come out there and make no mistakes and just be able to fly around and do what I do. I’m getting there, for sure." Chargers Sign Patrick Herbert to Practice Squad The Los Angeles Chargers signed tight end Patrick Herbert to their practice squad Monday, joining his brother, starting quarterback Justin Herbert, according to NFL Network. Patrick Herbert was waived by the Jacksonville Jaguars ahead of Sunday's 53-man roster deadline and chose Los Angeles after receiving interest from multiple teams. The Herbert brothers previously played together at Oregon during the 2019 season, helping lead the Ducks to a Rose Bowl victory. Patrick, who recorded two catches for 12 yards during Jacksonville's 2026 preseason action, joins a Chargers tight end group featuring Charlie Kolar, Oronde Gadsden, and David Njoku. The Chargers open the regular season on Sept. 13 against the Arizona Cardinals. Injury News & Notes

articles.title: 7 QBs in Round 1 of the NFL Draft? You can't rule it out in what could be a deep well of college talent
articles.summary: There's enough talent in college football to threaten the all-time NFL draft mark for first-round quarterbacks in 2027.
articles.body:
The NFL Draft Class of 1983 stood as the benchmark for years as a record six quarterbacks landed in the first round.

Forty-one years later, the mark was matched, with six more QBs landing in Round 1, and all of them in the first 12 selections.

Is a higher bar achievable? Could the Class of 2027 break the QB draft record?

"Gut feeling, no," an AFC scouting director told Yahoo Sports. "There's a lot that has to happen for it to all work out like that. You need six or seven who are close to first-round value. You probably have to have one or two really break out this season.

"You also need the teams [needing quarterbacks]. Most teams won't wait for the draft to get their [quarterback]. It might take 10 or 12 looking to get there because they won't all get [a veteran QB]."

Another veteran talent evaluator chimed in: "I've been saying since 2018 [when there were five first-round quarterbacks] that having seven or eight one day wouldn't shock me. The talent has to match the need — you need teams up there looking for one — but it's possible."

The Browns and Jets top the 2027 team-needs list for QB now. The Cardinals, Dolphins and Steelers could join them. Two teams that drafted QBs in 2024, the Falcons and Vikings, can't be ruled out as possibilities. Longer-shot options include the Colts and Commanders if their starters continue to be injury-plagued.

There also could be an unexpected team in the mix. The Colts never expected to draft Andrew Luck prior to 2012. The Cardinals selected Josh Rosen 10th overall in 2018, then Kyler Murray first overall the next year. The Bears drafted three first-round QBs in a seven-year span. Strange things happen every year in the draft.

"Could it be close? Six might not be crazy by the time we get to April, maybe even seven, I guess," the AFC director said. "I just don't think we're quite there yet."

Here's a look at the top quarterbacks prospects in what appears to be a deep group prior to the start of the 2026 college football season.

If Manning had a different last name, he might be a tougher sell as the odds-on favorite to be next year's top overall NFL Draft pick. But it's not completely pedigree-driven, either.

The 6-foot-4, 219-pound Manning is a terrific athlete with better raw traits than uncles Peyton or Eli. He weaponizes his skills as a runner and as a pressure evader. Manning can throw from different angles and platforms.

The second half of his 2025 season showed why and how Manning could be the top pick. After a clunky start early in the year, Manning cleaned up his lower-body mechanics, delivered more on-target throws (even as his receivers were guilty of some big drops) and made better decisions on when to scramble.

He's now blessed with a dream offensive cast, including the addition of wideout Cam Coleman, a possible top-10 pick. Manning still needs more experience (15 starts) but appears to be the clear favorite for the top pick if things continue along the current trajectory.

Moore might have been a first-round pick had he come out this year, with many feeling he would have been a strong candidate for the second overall pick behind Fernando Mendoza.

Moore is less physically blessed than Manning but he has more experience (20 starts) and might be the better touch passer with more natural accuracy. His intermediate and deep touch both grade out well above average, even approaching greatness. Moore's easy release and quiet feet will be appreciated by NFL quarterback coaches.

There are times, however, when Moore caves under pressure. Shaky moments against Penn State, Indiana (both games) and Texas Tech revealed concerns while dealing with pass-rush heat and muddled pockets.

Moore's talent appears strong this season, but there are questions on Oregon's offensive line, with only two returning starters and losing three to the NFL this spring.

A wild card with enticing skills, Mestemaker is this year's fastest riser. He never started a game in high school and was prepared to take the junior college route before being offered a walk-on spot at North Texas. Two years later he led FBS in passing yards, and he's now followed his head coach, Eric Morris, to Stillwater with a chance to develop into something special.

The 6-4, 210-pound Mestemaker has a big, loose arm and is willing to throw to all parts of the field. He'll carry the ball a little low at times but has the zip to thread passes on a line, and he routinely throws receivers open with anticipation. A lot of the Mean Green offensive talent will be following him to OSU, including RB Caleb Hawkins and WRs Wyatt Young and Miles Coleman, giving Mestemaker and Morris an instant comfort level.

Mestemaker remains raw, and he still could add some muscle and body armor to a slightly leaner frame, but the tools are all there. One area scout who saw him up close compared him to Ryan Tannehill, even if Mestemaker might not be quite as gifted a runner.

This could be a Fernando Mendoza-esque rise for Mestemaker this season. Scouts know plenty about him, just as they did Mendoza at this time a year ago. With a few more questions answered, the sky is the limit. OSU's press box should be filled with NFL talent evaluators in Week 2, when Oregon and Dante Moore arrive for what should be one of the best QB showdowns of the season.

Carr had a terrific redshirt freshman season, showing rare poise for a young player and the ability to push the ball downfield. He's a polished and natural thrower with respectable athletic traits, and he largely kept the ball out of harm's way.

Some talent evaluators see a high-floor prospect who demonstrated NFL-caliber processing as a freshman. Others view Carr more conservatively, wondering if there's much upward mobility in his game, appearing to lack a special athletic trait.

Another season of starting should reveal exactly where Carr's game is. Notre Dame is a strong team on the whole, but this is not an offense that can match talent, pound-for-pound, with the likes of Ohio State or Texas.

Carr was buoyed by one of the strongest run games in college football, and he lost first-round RBs Jeremiyah Love and Jadarian Price, along with two targets, WR Malachi Fields and TE Eli Raridon, who were drafted in Round 3. The Irish offensive line appears to be a strength, but the lack of clear-cut difference-makers at the skill positions will give us a window into how much Carr can elevate an offense.

Sellers is a great reminder about QB hype: It doesn't always go the way we expect. One year ago, the 6-4, 245-pound Sellers was being touted as a possible 1.1 pick in the draft, oozing with talent and as physically blessed as they come.

Neither of those statements are untrue now. He remains unique and a true dual-threat talent with NFL skills. They've just been tempered after a sideways 2025 season with the Gamecocks.

Sellers never quite locked in, struggling with missing layup-type throws, taking bad sacks and sometimes making life too difficult for himself. Some of his issues can be blamed on a chaotic offensive situation last season, one that the Gamecocks hope will be mitigated with some additions and new coordinator Kendal Briles.

If Sellers can get back to the level of playmaking he achieved in 2024 while reducing those mistakes by a tick, there's a clear path back to the first round.

Chambliss became one of college football's best stories last season, replacing an injured Austin Simmons and leading the Rebels to 11 wins in his first 12 starts. He arrived from Ferris State as a relative unknown in Oxford, but Chambliss became a folk hero by season's end, all the way down to the dramatic playoff loss to Miami.

Chambliss was a star in Division II, and his ability to create translated shockingly well in the SEC. He threw only three interceptions in 445 pass attempts, averaged 8.8 yards per attempt and was a menace with his legs, delivering at least one double-digit-yard run in 11 different games.

Working against Chambliss are his size and age. At just about 6 foot and 208 pounds, he'd be undersized by NFL standards. Chambliss will be 25 years old at draft time and will turn 26 late next preseason. That held a similarly aged Tyler Shough back in the 2025 NFL Draft, where he was selected 50th overall. Chambliss also can get happy feet and his accuracy will escape him through stretches, and there's no doubt that Ole Miss' talent and scheme helped him. How Chambliss fares without Lane Kiffin will be revealing, but Chambliss is an intriguing prospect who caught the NFL's attention last fall and will be on radars again.

Similar to Carr, Mensah is a high-level passer with average to above-average traits. Good, not great arm. Decent size. Capable athleticism. He doesn't possess a single physical quality that makes you leap out of your chair, but he's not deficient in any of those areas, and his impressive feel for the passing game more than compensates.

Mensah is a comfortable, efficient thrower who will spray the ball all over the field, but he's especially adept at attacking the middle of the field, whether it's threading passes into tight windows or layering throws over the top. He has a clean release and operates with good rhythm when he's given time.

Mensah also can play fast because he appears to process quickly, although he will throw some passes up for grabs that make you hold your breath. With a terrific surrounding cast at Miami and some softer defenses on the schedule, he should be in line for a big season after leaving Duke for a major NIL package from the Hurricanes. Is it enough to push him into the Day 1 discussion? Perhaps.

Sayin is another highly efficient pocket passer with excellent feel, especially for his limited experience. You also can't understate the pressure he faced last season in the cauldron that is Columbus. They expect a lot out of their quarterbacks there, especially with the receiver and O-line talent the Buckeyes almost always have on hand.

Even while he was surrounded by NFL-caliber talent, Sayin operated at a high level far more often than not last season as a redshirt freshman starting for the first time. He finished fourth in the Heisman Trophy balloting and led the Buckeyes to the Big Ten title game and the College Football Playoff.

At 6-1 and 214 pounds, Sayin is average-sized, or a bit below, and his raw arm talent appears closer to good than special. He also offers little utility as a scrambler. But it's hard to find naturally athletic quarterbacks with poise, so Sayin will have a chance. He's been named an OSU captain, and more will be expected of him in Year 2, but with elite offensive talent around him, it should be another huge statistical season for Sayin.

Lindsey isn't yet a first-round prospect, but he has the tools to get there. At 6-5 and 230 pounds, he has the frame you're looking for. His arm appears strong enough to push the ball vertically with ease, but Lindsey also displays nice touch on his throws, even on the move.

NFL teams will like that Lindsey appeared comfortable from both shotgun and under-center snaps, and he has displayed good toughness when standing in the pocket to deliver tough throws. Pressure doesn't seem to rattle him all that much, and it occasionally brings out the best in him.

Lindsey can take a read-option keeper for positive yards, but he might never be a true running threat in the NFL. His pocket movement can appear a bit clunky at times, and he'll resort to some off-balance throws. There are some mechanical elements that could be cleaned up. The Iowa and New Mexico games revealed a propensity for attempting risky throws. But there's a lot to work with here, and with a big season in his second year starting, Lindsey could receive a lot more attention from the NFL.

Bailey reminds me a bit of Jayden Daniels, who went from an intriguing, lean-framed quarterback to a top-tier NFL prospect in his final year at LSU. After taking a good step up from 2024 to 2025, Bailey easily could make similar improvements this season and become a fascinating prospect.

At nearly 6-6 and 218 pounds, Bailey is a tall, athletically blessed player who is still filling out his body. He's not as electric a runner as Daniels was, but Bailey is dangerous on designed runs and scrambles, especially in the red zone. He faced heavy pressure last season, but from about the Notre Dame game on, Bailey appeared to navigate it much better.

Unfortunately, he struggled badly in the opener at Virginia, losing an early fumble and throwing an interception in a 34-8 loss.

Bailey can make all the throws, and NFL teams will be intrigued with his skills, but so far the sum has not become better than the individual parts.

Leavitt is an adventurous experience to watch, delivering plenty of head-turning plays but also some head-scratching ones. If he can tone down his hyper-aggressiveness and harness his considerable tools, there might be a first-round case to be made.

Landing with Lane Kiffin at LSU is also a likely benefit, with a roster teeming with talent. The key for Kiffin will be to harness Leavitt's creativity and ability to create magic while also gently reeling him away from his happy feet or the devil-may-care throws Leavitt attempts too often. Bo Nix and Jaxson Dart are two examples of recent first-round quarterbacks who fine-tuned some of those plays out of their systems, which helped their draft hopes considerably.

Is Leavitt more backyard baller or true NFL passer? Some of that could be answered this season. There's still a debate about how good his arm really is and whether some of these bad habits can be coached out of him, but there aren't many better creators in college football.

The 6-6, 215-pound Iamaleava possesses elite athleticism and has a whippy, high-velocity arm — arguably one of the better natural throwers in college football.

As a thrower, he can drive the ball readily to the intermediate and deep parts of the field, attempting some throws other quarterbacks won't try. As a runner, Iamaleava ripped off 10 runs of 20-plus yards and kept defenses off-balance. There's a first-round tool kit in here, no question, with the Penn State and Michigan State tapes as the strongest evidence.

But the product has failed to match the individual parts often, especially after leaving Josh Heupel's QB friendly system at Tennessee. Iamaleava will succumb to pressure, take bad sacks and make ill-fated throws way too often. He's a first-round athlete with too much fifth-round tape. One big season in Westwood could considerably change his career arc.

Sorsby will not play college football this season following his gambling scandal that prevented him from taking a snap at Texas Tech. It's hard to envision a non-first-round prospect (most scouts issued him Day 2 grades or lower last cycle) suddenly becoming one without playing.

But if Sorsby can keep his nose clean, work hard on the side and perhaps show up raring to go at one of the postseason all-star games, a higher than expected draft slot wouldn't be shocking .

With a thick build, very good toughness and dual-threat ability, Sorsby has a lot of physical qualities NFL teams are looking for. He can operate off-platform and be effective as a runner.

Off-field questions and the interview process will be absolutely crucial for him next winter and spring, but the talent is there.

articles.title: B/R 99: Ranking the 99 Best Fantasy Football Seasons of All Time
articles.summary: When a fantasy manager lands a league-winning player, it's an event. A full season's worth of pure football joy and something to hold over leaguemates for years on end.
articles.body:
When a fantasy manager lands a league-winning player, it's an event . A full season's worth of pure football joy and something to hold over leaguemates for years on end.

It's one of the purest reasons to play this game we all love, allowing us to say, even if for just a short period: I made the better call.

Fantasy football is littered with these seasons in the decades since it became popular. To sort them all out, two-time Fantasy Sports Writers Association Football Writer of the Year Gary Davenport considered several factors, including total scoring in full-point-per-reception formats, average draft position, performance relative to positional peers and some good old-fashioned subjectivity from years in the fantasy game.

Since 1980, no one's done it better than this bunch.

Try the B/R Fantasy Picker and build your own all-time squad on a $15 budget.

The list kicks off with a grouping that features two of the lowest draft positions in our ranking. Baker Mayfield went 158th in 2024, and Cam Newton went 152nd in 2011. Each finished as QB3, which is roughly the bar for entry here.

Keep scrolling to explore the next tier.

Nine of the 10 players in this group had already finished among the top 12 at their positions the previous season. Most, however, were not the only players at their respective positions to post career years.

Still, this group is one of the clearest indicators that a player didn't have to win his position in a given year to make the list. Only four of these 10 did so, the fewest of any group from here on out.

The 1990s are well represented here: four of the 13 seasons from the magazine era (1987-98) land in this tier—Steve Young, Jerry Rice, Emmitt Smith and Barry Sanders.

It's also the tier with the most surprises, as Jimmy Graham, Steve Smith Sr. and rookie Edgerrin James were all off the fantasy radar the year prior.

There was lots of value to be had in this group. Seven of the 10 went off draft boards at pick 18 or later the year before, including 1999 Marvin Harrison after a WR32 season, 2017 Todd Gurley after finishing RB20 and 2021 Tom Brady following a QB8 finish.

There were exceptions, though, with 2021 Josh Allen, 2020 Travis Kelce and 2004 Tony Gonzalez all repeating as the top player at their respective positions.

Expectations were high in this group, and it turns out that drafters got it right. Six of the 10 went in the first 10 picks, and nearly all of them were top-12 at their position the year before.

This is also the most modern stretch in the rankings, as 2003 is as far back as this group goes.

No other tier covers more ground. It's the only one that touches all four eras of fantasy data, spanning from 1983 to 2025. The logic of the rankings shows in the spread, as 2022 Mahomes has the ninth-highest raw point total on the list, while the two tight ends sit in the 90s.

Position scarcity and era context carry as much weight here as anywhere on the board.

All 10 seasons in this group finished No. 1 at their respective positions, making it the first tier to feature a clean sweep—though not the last. In 1980, Kellen Winslow outscored the next-best player at his position by a larger margin than any other player on the list.

Speaking of that era, nearly half the list's pre-1987 entrants are packed into this group. Winslow, 1983 Eric Dickerson and 1985 Roger Craig make three of the seven representing fantasy's early days.

We arrive at the second consecutive group in which every player finished No. 1 at his position.

This time, the cost of admission varied wildly.

2015 Antonio Brown went third overall on average and 2001 Marshall Faulk went first, while 2011 Gronkowski (119) and 2015 Cam Newton (84) came off the board much later.

This tier illustrates the value that elite tight end and quarterback seasons can provide when managers identify breakout candidates at a discount.

This group features dominant seasons from a young Arian Foster in 2010 and a veteran Randy Moss in need of a change of scenery before his reemergence in 2007, both of whom were completely off the fantasy radar the previous year.

Elsewhere, both 2006 Steven Jackson and 2003 LaDainian Tomlinson were RB2 in those years, each finishing behind a player who had a top-10 season on our list.

Also of note, Dan Marino's 1984 is the earliest season in the top 20 and the highest ranked entry from before 1987.

The top 10 is exceptionally strong, and any one of these seasons could have delivered a fantasy league title. The five running backs in this tier were all top-five picks, underscoring the position's value. Even with that lofty draft status, they still exceeded expectations.

The other positions paint a different picture. The two quarterbacks in this tier—2018 Patrick Mahomes and 2019 Lamar Jackson—had ADPs near 100 and were afterthoughts the previous season. Cooper Kupp, the highest-ranked wide receiver, finished as WR34 in 2020 before his historic 2021 campaign.

2022 Kelce, the lone tight end in this group, ranked No. 87 in raw points among the 99 seasons. That was the largest disparity between a season's overall ranking and its raw-points ranking, illustrating the value of outperforming positional peers.

articles.title: Updated BR NFL1000 Team Rankings After 2026 Roster Cuts
articles.summary: The NFL's annual cutdown day is always difficult for everyone involved. Ultimately, the league's 53-man roster mandate is supposed to serve as a way to level the playing field, but not all active rosters are built the same.
articles.body:
The NFL's annual cutdown day is always difficult for everyone involved. Ultimately, the league's 53-man roster mandate is supposed to serve as a way to level the playing field, but not all active rosters are built the same.

Prior to the start of the preseason, Bleacher Report identified the league's most stacked rosters . A revisit was necessary after moves were made at this year's initial roster deadline.

Interestingly, the same 10 teams remain at the top. However, some of the positions shifted, with a noticeable trend in favor of those squads cutting graded players. Conversely, organizations that can move on from graded players demonstrate just how deep their rosters are.

The B/R NFL 1000 continues to serve as a barometer to determine which squads are the most talented based on how they're currently built. The following 10 teams have the highest concentration of top talent based on their average overall grade among those appearing on the list and how many of those individuals cracked B/R's Top 100.

Click here for a rundown of the full NFL 1000 series slate.

Average Grade : 71.8 Top 100 Players : 4 Highest-Rated : Josh Allen

Offensively, the Buffalo Bills know what they have. Quarterback Josh Allen is an annual MVP candidate. Running back James Cook Jr. returns as the league's leading rusher. DJ Moore was added to the mix this offseason, which increased the talent and depth at wide receiver. Buffalo's offensive line is experienced. The defense is primarily where question marks still exist. A lack of cornerback depth is concerning. Granted, CJ Gardner-Johnson and Jalon Kilgore present flexibility as safeties with plenty of experience covering the slot. Still, the team's pure cornerback options are thin at best. Furthermore, the transition to Jim Leonard's new scheme remains a work-in-progress. The Bills should be more aggressive overall. It's still not known whether all the right pieces are in place for this group to legitimately play strong complementary football.

Average Grade : 72 Top 100 Players : 4 Highest-Rated : Zach Frazier

The Pittsburgh Steelers will again hang their hat on a veteran-laden defense, with Cameron Heyward, T.J. Watt and Jalen Ramsey leading the way. The unit will also benefit from the investments made in Keeanu Benton, Nick Herbig, Jamel Dean and Jaquan Brisker.

The biggest changes to the roster from the start of training camp to the end of preseason came along the offensive line, where center Zach Frazier serves as the anchor.

Pittsburgh traded 2023 first-round pick Broderick Jones to the Dallas Cowboys after injuries clouded his future and the Steelers have a viable replacement in Troy Fautanu, who shifted from right to left tackle. The entire right side of the line will look different this fall.

Dylan Cook is expected to open the season at right tackle and hold down that spot until first-round rookie Max Iheanachor is ready. Spencer Anderson should be the new starting right guard as well. Even if some of the names are the same, three-fifths of the Steelers offensive line will be new this season.

Obviously, Pittsburgh has plenty of talent at multiple positions, but the Steelers could be held back by an aging quarterback playing behind a reworked front five.

Average Grade : 72 Top 100 Players : 5 Highest-Rated : Patrick Surtain II

The depth of a roster can often be ascertained by its rookie class. First-year players, particularly Day 3 draft picks, have a much harder time cracking a quality lineup.

Case in point, the Denver Broncos drafted seven players this past April. Three of them have already been cut. In fact, all but one of the team's draftees in the fifth round or later failed to make the roster.

The vast majority of Denver's roster returns from last season. The Broncos were one game away from making the Super Bowl. Significant changes weren't necessary. If anything, a young core of talent can continue to grow together.

Quarterback Bo Nix, running back RJ Harvey, wide receiver Troy Franklin, pass-rusher Nik Bonitto, safety Talanoa Hufanga and cornerbacks Patrick Surtain II, Riley Moss and Ja'Quan McMillian are all 26 or younger.

As that group develops, the Broncos expect bigger and better returns each season.

Average Grade : 72.2 Top 100 Players : 4 Highest-Rated : Jaxon Smith-Njigba

A pair of significant injuries could mar the early portion of the Seattle Seahawks' 2026 campaign. The organization already planned for one, but it doesn't necessarily have a fallback plan for the other.

Expectedly, Zach Charbonnet will open the season on the physically unable to perform list after suffering a torn ACL during the team's Super Bowl run. First-round rookie Jadarian Price will function as the Seahawks' lead back to open the campaign.

"He's done a great job. He really has—all three downs," head coach Mike Macdonald said, per ESPN's Brady Henderson . "He's a rookie in terms of, there's going to be things that we're going to attack in his game that will show itself in games. We haven't been afforded the luxury of having the bodies right now at running back to give him the reps in a [preseason] game that we would normally give to a rookie runner."

Conversely, last year's superstar rookie, Nick Emmanwori, may not be ready for Week 1 after requiring offseason ankle surgery. He is a legitimate difference-maker and valuable defensive piece thanks to his versatility. He can't be immediately replaced.

Otherwise, Sam Darnold moves into his second year as Seattle's starting quarterback. The squad's top wide receivers and starting offensive line remain intact. Maybe most importantly, the Seahawks' veteran defensive front still has Leonard Williams, Byron Murphy II and DeMarcus Lawrence to help dictate contests.

Four significant additions could change the face of this Baltimore Ravens squad (beyond the hire of head coach Jesse Minter).

Offensively, a pair of rookies should help to address significant need areas. The first-round selection of Olaivavega Ioane can provide a physical tone-setter along the offensive interior. With the loss of three-time Pro Bowl center Tyler Linderbaum in free agency, Ioane can now be the tip of the spear for Baltimore's front five.

Third-round wide receiver Ja'Kobi Lane was the most pleasant surprise from the Ravens' training camp. He is a big-bodied target to provide a different dynamic in the team's passing attack.

On the other side of the ball, Nnamdi Madubuike's expected return from a serious neck injury could provide a significant lift since he's one of the game's best interior pass-rushers.

Madubuike played in only two games last season before being sidelined. He's starting the 2026 campaign on Baltimore's active roster.

Finally, Trey Hendrickson's signing gives the squad the caliber of pass-rusher it's lacked for a long time.

Those four coupled with quarterback Lamar Jackson, running back Derrick Henry, tight end Mark Andrews, wide receiver Zay Flowers, linebacker Roquan Smith and safety Kyle Hamilton make the Ravens an AFC favorite if the group stays healthy.

Average Grade : 72.4 Top 100 Players : 6 Highest-Rated : Lane Johnson

Talent has never been in question with the Philadelphia Eagles. General manager Howie Roseman understands how to draft and stack a roster. This year's squad is all about whether the team actually jells. It didn't happen last season despite an 11-6 record and postseason berth. It's clear the Eagles have the capabilities of competing at a high level. High-end performers can be found throughout the lineup. Obviously, the AJ Brown trade changes the Eagles' aerial attack. However, the signing of Dontayvion Wicks and first-round selection of Makai Lemon give Philadelphia two more options beyond DeVonta Smith. Beyond signing Riq Woolen to upgrade the outside corner spot opposite Quinyon Mitchell, the Eagles have everything in place to succeed and possibly compete for another Super Bowl appearance. Even so, the team keeping four quarterbacks became the most interesting aspect coming out of training camp and the preseason. Jalen Hurts' erratic play proved to be rather limiting in 2025. The team now has veteran Andy Dalton and Tanner McKee backing up the incumbent. Plus Cole Payton is a developmental option. The Eagles are too talented overall to have their quarterback hold them back.

Average Grade : 72.4 Top 100 Players : 7 Highest-Rated : Jahmyr Gibbs

Even though the Detroit Lions now find themselves among the league's top four squads, the team did take a significant hit during training camp when center Cade Mays suffered a fractured wrist.

Mays is expected back this season after being placed on injured reserve with a designation to return. Still, his absence will be felt. Detroit features significant offensive talent, specifically quarterback Jared Goff, running back Jahmyr Gibbs and wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown. But the offense is built on a strong offensive line.

Now, the O-line is questionable. Penei Sewell is making the switch from right to left tackle. Rookie Blake Miller takes over at right tackle. The coaching staff was experimenting with options to take over at center leading into the regular season. Detroit did acquire Juice Scruggs, as part of the David Montgomery trade, to help offset the injury loss.

Beyond that specific concern, the Lions lineup is far better than last season's 9-8 record indicates. This group may not be 15-2 good, but it's likely closer to what it was two seasons ago than last year, mainly due to the hire of Drew Petzing as offensive coordinator and Kelvin Sheppard being more experienced as the defensive play-caller.

Average Grade : 72.8 Top 100 Players : 5 Highest-Rated : Myles Garrett

The Los Angeles Rams are a legitimate wild card in these rankings. They're ranked third without a designation for Aaron Donald, who just came out of retirement and re-signed with the team.

For transparency's sake, Donald wouldn't have received a grade from the B/R Scouting Department, because he hasn't played since the 2023 campaign. No one knows exactly the caliber of performer returning to the Rams. Though most expect him to be a quality performer once again, even if the 35-year-old is no longer competing to win a fourth NFL Defensive Player of the Year award.

There's a world where Donald is still an excellent player even if he takes a couple of steps back. If so, the Rams could realistically be the No. 1 team among these rankings. Even without him, the roster is loaded.

Myles Garrett is the No. 1 overall player on the B/R NFL 1000. Matthew Stafford is the league's reigning MVP. An argument can be made in favor of Puka Nacua as the game's top wide receiver. The defensive front also features Byron Young, Kobie Turner and Braden Fiske. Plus, general manager Les Snead upgraded the secondary this offseason with the acquisitions of Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson.

As a result, the Rams continue to receive significant Super Bowl hype and deservedly so.

Average Grade : 73 Top 100 Players : 6 Highest-Rated : Fred Warner

The San Francisco 49ers' regular-season roster benefited the most from new rankings. They moved from ninth to second after making cuts and nearly caught the No. 1 team. This movement shows how strong San Francisco's talent core really is.

The last point should come as no surprise. San Francisco has regularly featured some of the league's best rosters since John Lynch became general manager and Kyle Shanahan took over as head coach.

Injuries have been the franchise's bugaboo, and the 49ers defense will rely heavily on Nick Bosa, Mykel Williams and Fred Warner this year. All three are coming off of significant season-ending injuries. Conversely, the squad shouldn't count on Christian McCaffrey as much as last season. He's now 30 coming off a 400-plus-touch campaign.

The talent is readily available and obvious, with Brock Purdy, Trent Williams and George Kittle to go along with those already mentioned.

To the organization's credit, it still signed Mike Evans, re-signed Deebo Samuel and drafted De'Zhaun Stribling to rework the wide receiver room. Fourth-round rookie Carver Willis could be a first-year starter at left guard. Dre Greenlaw is back as well.

At the same time, a delicate balancing act (and a little luck) is necessary for the Niners to fully capitalize during this window.

Average Grade : 73.1 Top 100 Players : 6 Highest-Rated : Derek Stingley Jr.

The Houston Texans remain in the top spot after reducing their roster to the 53-man limit. But the organization wasn't content with what it already had on the roster. Instead, general manager Nick Caserio swung a pair of low-level but possibly significant trades at the deadline.

Obviously, the Texans will be built around their defense. Will Anderson Jr., Danielle Hunter, Derek Stingley Jr., Jalen Pitre and Calen Bullock are all standouts. No opponent wants to face this group. However, the Texans can't be considered legitimate contenders until their offense proves itself, starting with C.J. Stroud.

In order for the quarterback to thrive, the Texans did what they could to solidify their offensive line and improve his surrounding cast. This offseason, Houston brought in running back David Montgomery, as well as offensive linemen Wyatt Teller, Braden Smith and first-round rookie Keylan Rutledge. The team didn't stop there.

Caserio traded for wide receiver Kayshon Boutte and offensive tackle Nate Thomas this week. Boutte finished second on the New England Patriots last season with six touchdown receptions. He also averaged 16.7 yards per catch—which topped everyone on the Texans. Meanwhile, Thomas made four starts at left tackle for the Dallas Cowboys, giving Houston more experienced depth.

The Texans may be talented, but they haven't achieved anything of note. These types of fortifications are exactly what can keep a squad afloat and performing at a high level when its depth is challenged throughout a campaign.

articles.title: Texas State football: 5 things to know about Texas Longhorns in Week 1 matchup
articles.summary: Texas State football's 2026-27 season kicks off Saturday against the Texas Longhorns, perhaps its toughest matchup of the season.
articles.body:
Texas State football's 2026-27 season kicks off Saturday against the Texas Longhorns, perhaps its toughest matchup of the season. Texas coach Steve Sarkisian spoke to the media Monday, sharing his thoughts on his program's preparedness and Texas State's rising status through the college ranks.

"A ton of respect for GJ Kinne and the job he's done at Texas State," Sarkisian said. "They're elevated as a program. They're now in the Pac-12, and he's got a really good football team."

Here's what to know about the Longhorns before Saturday's game.

Four Longhorns might be selected in the first round of the 2027 NFL Draft.

That list starts with quarterback Arch Manning, the nephew of former NFL quarterbacks Eli and Peyton Manning . He struggled as a starter last year before finding his groove in the back half of the season, throwing for 3,163 yards, 26 touchdowns and seven interceptions while completing 61.4% of his passes. The Athletic's Nick Baumgardner has him going No. 1 overall in his preseason 2027 NFL mock draft.

Left tackle Trevor Goosby, edge rusher Colin Simmons and wide receiver Cam Coleman also are projected to go within the top 10 picks of the mock draft.

Texas fired defensive coordinator Pete Kwiatkoski after last season, hiring former South Carolina and Florida head coach (and also former UT defensive coordinator) Will Muschamp as his replacement.

The Longhorns speak highly of Muschamp, who demands physicality and accountability in his practices. Sarkisian has praised the coach's defensive mind and brought him in to field a "more aggressive defense." This entails fewer schemes designed to limit big plays and more press coverage designed to stop easy, short completions.

Sarkisian said that aggressiveness does not entail recklessness. Even so, he's not naive to the idea that the adjustment to the scheme might take some time.

"There'll be some growing pains, but that's OK, too. That's part of this process," Sarkisian said.

Texas took a step back in 2025, missing the College Football Playoff after two consecutive berths in 2023 and 2024. Sarkisian said Monday the previous year's roster was "probably a little too young around Arch." Texas responded by piecing together the No. 2-ranked transfer portal class, according to 247Sports' composite ratings.

Coleman highlights the group as a 6-foot-3, 201-pound wideout who can be Manning's true No. 1 target. The Longhorns also added two of the best running backs on the market - Hollywood Smothers and Raleek Brown - to bolster the rushing attack.

Linebackers Rasheem Biles and Justin Cryer were other huge wins after linebacker Anthony Hill Jr. left for the NFL.

Texas LT Trevor Goosby is questionable to play

Goosby opted to return to Austin for his redshirt junior season and is one of the nation's top left tackles. He suffered a knee injury two weeks ago, and while he's questionable for Saturday, Sarkisian said Goosby and left guard Laurence Seymore III practiced Monday.

"Both Trevor and Laurence practiced today, and I thought they both looked really good," Sarkisian said.

If the two are unable to play, Andre Cojoe will start at left tackle and Dylan Sikorski at left guard.

Sarkisian, Kinne have different philosophies

Kinne and Sarkisian are two of the best play-calling head coaches in the country. But though both coach in the Lone Star State, they run vastly different schemes.

Texas leans into a pro-style approach. Sarkisian has spent time in the NFL and uses a variation of the West Coast offense pioneered by Bill Walsh. Meanwhile, Kinne is from the Gus Malzahn coaching tree. Sarkisian compared Texas State's offense to Tennessee and LSU, mentioning the up-tempo approach and the wide receivers' big splits.

"It's tough to defend. It's unique in that way that you're not facing it every week, and so you've got to spend a little time to get ready for it," Sarkisian said.

articles.title: Ranking The 10 Best 2027 NFL Draft Prospects — Who Aren't Quarterbacks
articles.summary: The 2027 draft could be one of the strongest in years, potentially featuring several franchise-altering prospects at positions other than QB.
articles.body: No one knows for sure how things might change during the upcoming college football season, but early indications are that the 2027 NFL Draft will be the strongest in years. Quarterbacks — such as Texas’ Arch Manning, Oregon’s Dante Moore and Ohio State's Julian Sayin — have dominated the early buzz because, well, they’re quarterbacks brimming with talent and potential. But the beauty of next year's draft class is that it could offer several franchise-altering prospects at other positions, as well. I’ve ranked the top 10 non-QBs heading into the season and, as you’d expect, all of them have a realistic chance at being a first-round pick next spring. Frankly, the top seven players would have been selected on Day 1 this year. As a bonus, I've included a pro comparison for each prospect. 10. Cayden Green, OT, Missouri Grading offensive linemen is more about fit and grit than analytics, but Green checks in with the numbers that even a stat geek can appreciate. The 6-foot-5, 324-pounder is a three-year starter dating back to his true freshman season at Oklahoma. He allowed just two sacks in 751 pass drops last year, his first at the premium left tackle position after spending his first two seasons inside at left guard, where he routinely delivered pancake blocks. Green is a talented pass blocker, as well as a spark plug in the running game. He gains impressive depth in his kick-slide and has the lateral agility and core strength to handle counters. I’m eager to see if he is even smoother in Year 2 at tackle. Between his girth, grip-strength, competitiveness and previous experience at guard, Green should offer his future NFL team plenty of roster flexibility. Pro comp: Dion Dawkins, Buffalo Bills 9. Kewan Lacy, RB, Ole Miss Lacy went from a backup at Missouri to leading the entire country with 24 rushing touchdowns at Ole Miss last year. He is sudden and slippery, consistently zipping around and past would-be tacklers. His elusiveness generates plenty of highlight-reel worthy plays, but Lacy is also quite effective in short yardage, showing impressive leg drive, balance through contact and sheer determination to grind out the tough yards, too. Along with his frequent trips to the end zone, the 5-foot-11, 205-pounder led the nation with 335 touches in 2025. There is no denying that Lacy was aided by the creative playcalling of former Ole Miss head coach Lane Kiffin. With Kiffin now in Baton Rouge, scouts are curious to see if Lacy can duplicate his remarkable sophomore campaign. Pro comp: TreVeyon Henderson, New England Patriots 8. Ellis Robinson IV, CB, Georgia Robinson wasn’t quite as flashy as the aforementioned Lacy last year, but he was close, earning FWAA Freshman Defensive Player of the Year honors with four interceptions, tying for tops in the talent-rich SEC. Robinson is every bit the athletic phenom you’d expect as a former five-star recruit out of IMG Academy. He has a tight, low backpedal and easy hip turn to track receivers downfield, showing impressive balance and burst out of his breaks and legitimate recovery speed when necessary. He’s also a surprisingly scrappy tackler. A rarity for a young cornerback, Robinson’s hands might be even better than his feet. Robinson can get a bit grabby downfield, but refs often let him compete because he locates the ball well, showing impressive hand-eye coordination to either catch it himself or rake it out of the hands of the intended receiver at the final moment. Interceptions against state rival Georgia Tech and this one versus Charlotte show Robinson’s rare body control and extension to make tough grabs look easy. Pro comp: Trent McDuffie, Los Angeles Rams 7. A'Mauri Washington, DT, Oregon With all due respect to star quarterback Dante Moore, Washington is both literally and figuratively the biggest reason why Oregon has a chance to match Indiana from a year ago and win its first national championship in program history. He is the centerpiece of arguably the best defensive line in college football. Washington would have been a first-round pick last year but was one of several Ducks who chose to stay north for one more winter rather than migrate to the NFL. He is surprisingly quick and agile for someone listed at 6-foot-4, 330 pounds, and he already possesses NFL power, stacking and discarding would-be blockers like paper plates at a summer barbeque. And just ask No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza about Washington’s bull rush. Pro comp: Kenny Clark, Dallas Cowboys 6. Cam Coleman, WR, Texas If you thought the hype built up around Arch Manning last year was intense, just wait until this season, with the Longhorns set to stampede for a national title and dominate the first round of the 2027 draft. Coleman — the first of three Longhorns in this article — was lured to Austin from Auburn, where he caught a combined 93 receptions for 1,306 yards and 13 touchdowns over his first two seasons, despite a limited supporting cast. The stats on Coleman are good, but the tape is even better. He is already an established playmaker whose film screams first-round pick. His star could shine from another galaxy, however, now that he's working with Manning and Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian, one of the best offensive minds in the sport at any level. The 6-foot-3, 200-pound Coleman has the size and athleticism of a future No. 1 NFL receiver. He is an effortless mover who accelerates in a flash and changes directions fluidly. Better yet, he offers exceptional body control and sticky hands to make acrobatic catches even with defenders draped over him. Pro comp: George Pickens, Dallas Cowboys 5. Leonard Moore, CB, Notre Dame Cornerback is not universally regarded as one of the premium positions by NFL teams. Otherwise, Moore might rank even higher on this list, as his profile is spectacular. He is coming off of a unanimous All-American campaign as a true sophomore in which he recorded five interceptions and was a finalist for not only the Jim Thorpe Award as the nation’s top defensive back, but the Bronko Nagurski Award as the best overall defender in college football. Listed at 6-foot-2, 197 pounds, Moore has intimidating size for a cornerback. He has a smooth turning motion, seamlessly transitioning out of his backpedal into full gallop. He locates the ball well for a young player, instantly reading underneath routes and showing impressive downhill quickness to trigger back toward the quarterback. Moore has broken up and/or intercepted more passes (25) than he has allowed first downs (23) over his first two seasons of college football, and he's also a physical hitter, having forced three fumbles. These numbers are all the more impressive when considering Notre Dame often asked him to travel with the opponents’ top receiver, including playing out of the nickel. Pro comp: Christian Gonzalez, New England Patriots 4. Trevor Goosby, OT, Texas No disrespect to former Texas OT Kelvin Banks Jr. — the No. 9 overall pick by the New Orleans Saints in 2025 — but the Longhorns might have upgraded with the 6-foot-7, 325-pound Goosby succeeding Banks at left tackle. Pro Football Focus pinned three sacks (out of 492 reps in pass protection) on Goosby last year, but I don’t know that he was truly at fault for any of them. His tape was as clean as any blocker in the 2026 draft, and remember, there were nine blockers drafted in the first round this past spring. Goosby is still just growing into his body, but he already moves with such an exciting combination of grace and force that it is easy to project him as a future Pro Bowler, if not All-Pro. He eases off the snap in pass protection, sliding laterally and keeping himself square to the rusher. Goosby surges low and hard as a run blocker, as well, showing impressive bend, balance and power to move defenders in the running game. Pro comp: Laremy Tunsil, Washington Commanders 3. Dylan Stewart, Edge, South Carolina Stewart promises to be one of the most scrutinized non-quarterbacks of this draft class because he is remarkably gifted yet has not generated the eye-popping production his talent portends. He checks in at a prototypical 6-foot-5, 250 pounds, with long arms, which he already effectively uses to lock out and shed would-be blockers, as well as lasso ballcarriers from behind. As a pass-rusher, Stewart is sudden off the snap and has excellent core flexibility to dip under the reach of offensive tackles, greasing the edge and closing in a flash. He’s recorded 11.5 sacks over his first two seasons of SEC football, but his frequent pressures suggest his production could be twice that. Stewart’s blend of size and athleticism are exciting build blocks. He’s already quite strong and is technically sound with some refined pass rush techniques. He’s just growing into his frame and game, projecting as a future All-Pro caliber edge. Pro comp: Robert Quinn (retired) 2. Collin Simmons, Edge, Texas Similar in many ways to 2026 No. 5 overall selection Arvel Reese, Simmons is a malleable monster capable of starring off the edge or as an off-ball linebacker. He is as swift on the perimeter as any rusher in this class, accelerating off the ball like a receiver getting into his route. He isn’t just explosive, he’s flexible, slithering his way through waves of blockers. Watch his anticipation on this snap. The quarterback (and left tackle) had no chance. Moreover, Simmons is shockingly strong at 6-foot-3, 240 pounds. Like all great speed rushers, Simmons generates impressive power with the momentum he gains off his rush, often bulldozing through blockers nearly 100 pounds larger. He has recorded 21 sacks over his first two seasons — despite starting just 13 games. Simmons’ physical gifts are undeniable and will almost certainly earn him a top-five selection whenever he chooses to enter the draft. He isn’t a prospect without flaws, however. He’s been penalized a dozen times in just two collegiate seasons, with most of his penalties coming from mental errors, such as lining up in the neutral zone or unnecessary late hits on the quarterback. Even with the occasional hiccup, Simmons has the look of a future franchise cornerstone. Pro comp: Von Miller, Dallas Cowboys 1. Jeremiah Smith, WR, Ohio State It is difficult to discuss Smith and not venture into hyperbole. Ohio State’s track record for producing superstar NFL wide receivers has been well documented and Smith’s production over his first two years in Columbus is unprecedented even among them. His 2,558 receiving yards and 27 touchdowns during his first two seasons on campus aren't just records for an Ohio State receiver; they top all pass-catchers in Big Ten history. Along with current and future Hall of Famers Calvin Johnson, Julio Jones, Derrick Henry, Myles Garrett and Penei Sewell, Smith is one of a handful of players I’ve evaluated over my career who I believe were capable of playing in the NFL as true freshmen. At a rocked up 6-foot-3, 223 pounds, Smith can simply bully most defensive backs at the college level. His size and strength make him an ideal weapon in the red zone, where he shows good timing and hand-eye coordination to play above the rim. And he’s a legitimate vertical threat who accelerates smoothly and tracks the ball well over his shoulder. Smith is also excellent on slants and crossing routes, utilizing his frame to keep himself between the defender and the ball and showing good vision to rack up yardage after the catch. It is remarkable how many times he outruns pursuit angles or slips between defenders seemingly in position to stop him. We’ve often heard the expression "runaway freight train" used to describe running backs, but the characterization also applies to Smith at receiver. Comparisons to past size-speed phenoms such as the aforementioned Johnson, Jones and DK Metcalf will be common throughout the draft process. The scary part about Smith is that he’s already further along as a route-runner than any of these receivers were coming out of college. Pro comp: Julio Jones (retired)

articles.title: Brittany Mahomes grows her $15 million business empire with fitness ventures, activewear and a stake in the $325 million Kansas City Current
articles.summary: NFL News: Brittany Mahomes has built a business identity that extends well beyond being the wife of Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes. A former pro.
articles.body: Brittany Mahomes has built a business identity that extends well beyond being the wife of Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes. A former professional soccer player and certified personal trainer, she has turned her athletic background into several entrepreneurial opportunities, with fitness, fashion and women’s sports ownership at the center of her career.Brittany Lynne FitnessBrittany’s first major entrepreneurial venture came through Brittany Lynne Fitness, an online training platform she launched in 2019. With a bachelor’s degree in kinesiology from the University of Texas at Tyler and experience as a professional soccer player, Brittany used her knowledge of exercise and conditioning to create workout programs for people at different stages of their fitness journeys.The platform helped Brittany establish herself independently in the fitness space. Rather than simply promoting wellness products, she positioned herself as a trainer, creating programs designed around strength, conditioning and consistency.Sterling Skye ActivewearBrittany later expanded her presence in the fitness and fashion space through Sterling Skye, an activewear collaboration with Shop Vitality named after her daughter. The collection gave her fitness brand another avenue while combining athletic clothing with a personal family connection.The venture reflected Brittany’s broader approach to entrepreneurship: taking the interests that shaped her own life—fitness, sports and motherhood—and turning them into consumer-focused projects.Kansas City Current OwnershipPerhaps Brittany’s most significant business move has been her involvement with the Kansas City Current. She became a founding co-owner of the NWSL club in 2020, joining Angie and Chris Long in bringing professional women’s soccer back to Kansas City.Her investment is particularly meaningful because of her own soccer background. Brittany played collegiately before spending a season playing professionally in Iceland, giving her firsthand experience of the sport she is now helping build as an owner.The Current has since grown into one of the most prominent franchises in women’s soccer. Its home, CPKC Stadium, opened in 2024 as a purpose-built stadium for a professional women’s sports team, further highlighting the scale of the organization Brittany helped build.Patrick Mahomes later joined the Current’s ownership group, but Brittany’s involvement predates his investment.Brand Partnerships and Social MediaBrittany has also developed a significant commercial presence through social media, where her interests in fitness, fashion, family and sports have created opportunities for brand collaborations. Her public profile allows her to work with companies while maintaining the personal lifestyle brand she has developed over the years.Her appearance in Sports Illustrated Swimsuit has also expanded her visibility beyond the fitness and sports worlds. She made her debut in the magazine’s 2024 issue and returned for a 2026 digital cover.Building a Brand Beyond FootballBrittany Mahomes’ ventures show how she has built a career around her own experiences rather than relying solely on her husband’s NFL fame. From launching an online fitness business to investing in professional women’s soccer, her portfolio reflects her background as an athlete and her interest in empowering women in sports.While Patrick Mahomes has his own business ventures—including 1587 Prime—Brittany’s entrepreneurial story is distinctly her own. Her biggest business achievement may ultimately be the transformation of her passion for fitness and soccer into long-term ownership, branding and influence within the rapidly growing world of women’s sports.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
