articles.title: How Travis Kelce is taking his fashion game to the next level with $450 million designer Tommy Hilfiger
articles.summary: NFL News: Travis Kelce is entering the new NFL season with more than football on his mind. The Kansas City Chiefs tight end is now fronting a major Tommy Hilfig.
articles.body: Travis Kelce is entering the new NFL season with more than football on his mind. The Kansas City Chiefs tight end is now fronting a major Tommy Hilfiger campaign alongside names including Gigi Hadid, Jisoo, Peggy Gou, Frances Tiafoe and Carmelo Anthony. The project highlights a side of Kelce that has become increasingly hard to miss: his growing influence in fashion, entertainment and popular culture.Travis Kelce brings his personal style to Tommy HilfigerKelce’s partnership with Tommy Hilfiger feels especially fitting because the brand has been part of his fashion story since his younger years. He recalled asking his mother for a Tommy sailing jacket while he was in high school and said he always admired the label’s sportswear.That early connection now has a new chapter. Kelce is working with Hilfiger on a collection planned for spring 2027, giving him an opportunity to move from wearing the brand to helping shape its future designs.The NFL star has never been afraid to experiment with clothes. His wardrobe has included bold suits, statement accessories and eye-catching designer pieces. He credits athletes he admired growing up for helping shape that confidence.“My style interest started when I was a kid, through my love for sports,” he sayd as per Vogue. “The basketball shoes, the Ken Griffey Jrs, even Wayne Gretzky’s style in the late ’90s, when he teamed up with Nike. There are so many athletes I could name. Deion Sanders is another. He had so much swagger in how he dressed and presented himself. I think that’s where the interest started, and I’m a bit of a chameleon, you know? I kind of take bits and pieces from everybody and everything that I see, and just kind of change things around depending on which situation I’m in and what event I’m going to.”For Hilfiger, Kelce offers more than star power. His personality, sports background and genuine interest in clothing make him a natural fit for the brand.Travis Kelce balances NFL career with life beyond footballThe fashion campaign comes as Kelce prepares for his 14th NFL season with the Chiefs. He has already collected three Super Bowl victories with the franchise and remains focused on adding more success to his career.“Year 14, baby, I’m fired up,” he says. “Every year there’s a chance to do something special—but especially coming into this year, getting Pat [Mahomes] back and wiping the slate clean. I love coming to the building every day. I know how special this team is, so I’m excited to get this thing rolling and for the chance to give the fans what they deserve.”Away from the field, Kelce has built an entertainment profile through his podcast New Heights, which he hosts with his brother Jason, as well as his appearance on Saturday Night Live. His relationship with Taylor Swift has also pushed his public profile to another level, while his fashion choices continue to attract attention.Even with that growing spotlight, Kelce says home remains important. When he gets time away from football, his ideal day is simple: golf, a nap, good food and time with family.That mix of elite football, entertainment appeal and an increasingly confident fashion identity has made Kelce one of the NFL’s most recognizable figures beyond the sport itself.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Fantasy Football: NFL coaching and coordinating changes we like, are just 'fine' and those we're skeptical about
articles.summary: These changes are set make massive fantasy football impacts in 2026.
articles.body:
The following was borrowed from Matt Harmon's 2026 Draft Blueprint, the definitive resource for your draft prep. Click here to check out the full piece .

If you know me, I am all about ecosystems. Fantasy football can be all about hammering players from the best ecosystems in the NFL. I always think back to the Peyton Manning-Broncos teams circa 2013. Sometimes winning your fantasy league is as simple as hoarding as many players from those kinds of special offenses.

It's obvious that great ecosystems equate to some of the most potent and efficient offenses in the NFL. They're surrounded by a quality line, loaded with good skill position talent and stewarded by a high-end play-caller. But there's more to it than that. It helps if you have concentrated target trees and clear backfield usage, but you shouldn't just cross off teams that don't fit the bill. Ambiguous situations can still equal profit.

If anything, the lesson from last season was how much great play-callers and offensive designers matter. Teams like the Jaguars and Bears reached unseen heights with the additions of Liam Coen and Ben Johnson as play-calling head coaches. The Patriots got back on track with Josh McDaniels taking over the scoring unit. Even a team like New Orleans became the source of sneaky value down the stretch with Kellen Moore installing a progressive offense that ranked first in presnap motion. Most importantly, the teams that Johnson, Moore and Coen left behind in 2025 all experienced some regression offensively.

Players make the plays but great coaches lay the soil for those trees to grow.

NFL teams know the value of a great coach on offense, as over half the league turned over their play-callers from 2025 to 2026. Everyone wants their version of Johnson, Coen or, in the most ideal world, Sean McVay, right now. With all the coaching turnover, I wrote up a piece back in February sorting the new hires into buckets based on how much I liked the move for fantasy football . Revisit that for the full analysis, but here, we will revisit the groupings ('I like it,' 'it's fine,' 'I'm skeptical') with some quick and updated thoughts on how those offenses project.

A hire that was met with skepticism, but frankly, I thought was a huge win; LaFleur is ready to at least be the architect of an offense. He was better than credited as the Jets' offensive coordinator, leaning into the right schematic buttons that boost modern offenses. I am Cardinals Curious and believe this team will be better offensively than the fantasy hivemind thinks, despite long-term quarterback questions.

Ravens hire HC Jesse Minter, OC Declan Doyle will call plays

Doyle is a young and intriguing hire off the Sean Payton and Ben Johnson coaching tree. We are likely to see something similar to what the Bears ran in 2025. Expect plenty of zone rushing and play action on downfield route concepts.

The Bills promoting Brady likely keeps more of the same in place with the Bills. I'm higher on Brady than most in the space. Many of the outside complaints about Brady's offense — heavy use of mesh, tons of screens/short throws and a tendency to go run-heavy — are mostly forced into the unit because of personnel problems. I expect the addition of DJ Moore and perhaps getting the running backs more involved in the passing game, as has been reported from camp, will solve a lot of that.

It may not all come together for fantasy football in 2026 but this was a great hire. Kubiak did almost everything you want out of a modern offensive coordinator last season. Seattle made use of heavy personnel packages to increase the efficiency of the passing game, ran under-center play action and was fifth in dropback motion rate. He's also not a one-hit wonder, as he was doing most of this for a 2024 Saints team that had its moments offensively but fell apart due to injuries. Let's just hope Ashton Jeanty will be on the field to reap the benefits of this new system.

Just like everyone else, I'm excited about the idea of adding Mike McDaniel as offensive coordinator to an already strong team under Jim Harbaugh and a talented offense. If you're interested in chasing the hype, however, expect to pay a heavy ADP price. The pursuit may well be worth it. We've never seen McDaniel's offense operated by a quarterback as talented as Justin Herbert and this team is quietly loaded at all skill position spots. Unfortunately, the offensive line is dealing with injuries yet again.

Falcons hire HC Kevin Stefanski, OC Tommy Rees will call plays

I'll admit I'm mixed on this one and the quarterback situation makes it even murkier. However, I think Stefanski is a quality offensive coach and his scheme does fit with Atlanta's talent. He's a sensible option but might not be a true needle-mover like some of these other names. Rees is also an unproven variable and I wouldn't say anything from recent Browns seasons push my opinion one way or another.

Blough coached under Kliff Kingsbury the last two seasons, but I expect he will present a somewhat left-turn schematically from the spread tenets of that offense. Blough began his career in 2019 with the Detroit Lions as a backup quarterback and hung on to the roster through Ben Johnson's rise up the ranks from offensive quality control coach, tight ends coach and ultimately to a passing game coordinator role in 2021, where, after Anthony Lynn was demoted, he helped head coach Dan Campbell bring to life what we now identify as the Lions offense. Blough would return to Detroit in one of Johnson's final seasons with the club as the offensive coordinator when he was no doubt already eyeing a move to the coaching ranks. My suspicion was that Blough probably leans more toward the ideas of Johnson's scheme.

Monken has head coaching experience at Southern Mississippi from 2013 to 2015 and has most recently been the architect of a Ravens offense that ranked third in EPA per play and fourth in success rate since his arrival in 2023. While Lamar Jackson deserves a good chunk of that credit, there's no doubt that Monken helped evolve the MVP quarterback's game. His presence with this team makes me more optimistic when selecting the pass-catchers despite obvious quarterback questions surrounding named-starter Deshaun Watson and big-name backup Shedeur Sanders.

The Lions picking Drew Petzing for the offensive coordinator job got flamed on the internet but just as the section implies, I thought the hire was … just fine. To be clear, there are some justifiable critiques of his play-calling work and pre-snap alignment of Marvin Harrison Jr. and Michael Wilson with the Cardinals, and those are areas where the 38-year-old needs to improve. However, my hunch is he's mostly in Detroit to revive its run game, which stalled out last year under John Morton, while the passing game principles held by Dan Campbell will remain the same.

Slowik became a bit of a punching bag by the end of his watch as the Texans offensive coordinator in 2024, but I think he's worth a second look at the position. Slowik couldn't evolve the offense as the team had hoped from the "The Shanahan Greatest Hits" compilation it ran in 2023 to a more three-receiver spread unit in 2024. However, he did good work in that first year and was on this Dolphins staff last season. I can't imagine he's going to come in here and tear down a successful run game, which matters for De'Von Achane, the only Miami player drafted highly in fantasy.

Two noteworthy takeaways come from Seattle's hiring of Brian Fleury. For starters, it's interesting that Seattle, which had some internal candidates to replace Klint Kubiak, decided to go outside the building and pluck another Shanahan tree member. The second is that Fleury, who was most recently the tight ends coach in San Francisco since 2022 and held the title of run game coordinator last year, has an extremely varied background. My hunch is that Seattle won't change much of its stripes, but will hope Fleury can keep beefing up the run game — good news for Jadarian Price.

You can think what you want about Robinson's overall offensive attack in Atlanta. It wasn't perfect. However, he was objectively good for receiver usage, most notably when his motion concepts allowed all four of the main pass-catchers to get a 39% or higher slot rate on passing downs in 2024. This usage awaits for Emeka Egbuka, someone I'm drafting with a ton of confidence if healthy.

Brian Daboll has quarterback-development skins on the wall he can point to during his recent stints with the Bills and Giants. However, you can also argue that the Bills got better offensively when they moved away from his heavy spread concepts after he departed and Daniel Jones played his best football in a much better-designed unit last year with the Colts. My quick take on Daboll is that he helps get your quarterback on base, but his spread-and-shred stylings lead to way too much long-term volatility. For Tennessee and Cam Ward, getting on base would be progress.

Broncos promote OC Davis Webb, give him play-calling duties

The Broncos clearly felt the heat from what was a relatively hot cycle of interest in their 31-year-old former quarterback coach, Davis Webb. From what I hear, Webb and Bo Nix have a tight connection and this move likely signals their desire to help the young passer take the next step. That should be doable in 2026, especially with Jaylen Waddle in tow. I do wonder if Sean Payton doesn't get back in the play-calling chair at some point if this gets off to a slow start.

I like the idea of Mannion bringing in some tenets from Green Bay and that offensive family. It can help smooth out some of the rough edges in Philly's passing game from last year. But it's a big change for the Eagles based on how they've played under Jalen Hurts. It will be a lot to oversee for the 33-year-old riser, who was on NFL rosters as a player as recently as 2023 and spent the last two years with the Packers as an offensive assistant and then quarterback coach.

Giants hire HC John Harbaugh, OC Matt Nagy will call plays

The Chiefs essentially fired Matt Nagy. They can try to soften and launder it through the media, but they let him walk out the door without a thought of keeping him before he took a coordinator job in February, only after the Giants didn't land Monken. That's a firing and based on how it went in Kansas City, I don't blame them for wanting to make a change. I also find the fit with Jaxson Dart a little odd.

I don't think Mike McCarthy is some miserable hire by the Steelers, but I think we can agree it was uninspiring and likely doesn't push them out of the stagnation that befell them during the late Tomlin years. I have two major hang-ups about McCarthy as the offensive architect in Pittsburgh. For starters, it's tough that this is being framed as a way to make Aaron Rodgers, who was a bottom-tier quarterback last year, more comfortable. Second, it's hard not to notice that the Packers and even the 2025 Cowboys immediately got better right after McCarthy left, as a younger play-caller took over and installed a more dynamic offense with under-center concepts and more motion.

At least we have a clear idea of what the attack will look like under McCarthy. He'll cede plenty of pre-snap control to Rodgers and likely run an old West Coast offense out of mostly 11 personnel. Expect a lot of quick game to Michael Pittman Jr. and the occasional boundary shot to DK Metcalf.

Honestly, I didn't get this one. Tanner Engstrand designed a good passing game, but the sequencing and rushing attack in 2025 wasn't ideal. If you want to start over, that's fine, but I'm not sure Reich, who felt out of step with the league in his static RPO-heavy offense with the Panthers before a midseason firing in 2023, is the answer. The Jets quietly have a good group of weapons, but color me skeptical this will be what unlocks them.

articles.title: De’Zhaun Stribling takes Daejon Love’s No. 7 - Are 49ers players secretly embracing the fake NFL star story?
articles.summary: NFL News: The Daejon Love story has found another surprising connection to the San Francisco 49ers.Rookie wide receiver De’Zhaun Stribling has changed his jerse.
articles.body: The Daejon Love story has found another surprising connection to the San Francisco 49ers.Rookie wide receiver De’Zhaun Stribling has changed his jersey number from No. 15 to No. 7 - and that happens to be the number associated with Love during his alleged impersonation of a 49ers player. Not just any player, but a wide receiver. The same story of Stribling- who’s also a wideout for the Niners.The coincidence was quickly noticed online after NFL Insider Ari Meirov reported the change, pushing fans to connect Stribling’s new number with one of the strangest stories currently surrounding the NFL.There is no evidence that Stribling switched as a tribute to Love. Players change jersey numbers for countless reasons. But the timing has unequivocally created an irrefutable question for NFL fans: why does it feel like Daejon Love’s fake player story is slowly becoming a trendsetter?De’Zhaun Stribling’s No. 7 change reignites Daejon Love controversyStribling’s jersey number change might usually be little more than an offseason footnote.Instead, No. 7 has suddenly become a reminder of Love’s bizarre connection to the San Francisco 49ers.According to federal prosecutors, Love allegedly created a false identity as a professional football player and used that persona as part of a scheme that allegedly defrauded over 26 women of approximately $1.3 million. The allegations have generated widespread attention because Love reportedly presented himself as an NFL organization.That is what makes the No. 7 connection sound so weird!Stribling is an actual San Francisco 49ers rookie competing for a roster spot. Love, according to prosecutors, allegedly built an entirely fictional NFL identity over four years.Two completely different stories have now collided around the same jersey number.Are NFL players secretly loving the Daejon Love story?The bigger question isn’t really whether Stribling supports Love. There is nothing publicly establishing that.Instead, the interesting part is how the Love story has become a social media phenomenon that even ordinary NFL developments can accidentally bring it back into the spotlight with a bang.Fans have turned the Daejon Love story into memes, jokes, and endless online commentary. Every unusual connection to the 49ers seems to offer another opportunity for the story to resurface and stay on the surface.That definitely does not mean NFL players are wholeheartedly supporting Love - or approving of the alleged scheme.If anything, the fascination seems to come from the sheer absurdity of someone allegedly constructing an entire fake professional football identity with unbelievable audacity.The league is filled with larger-than-life personalities, but pretending to be an NFL player while allegedly using that identity to deceive people takes sports fandom to an unimaginable level.Stribling’s number change simply gave cyberspace another entry into the Love story.Why Daejon Love’s fake NFL player story won’t go away?The Love controversy has all the spices of a viral sports story: the 49ers, a mysterious fake identity, alleged financial deception, fake romance, and now a never-heard-before jersey No. connection.But serious allegations shouldn’t get lost beneath the funny memes.Love has been accused by federal authorities of impersonating an NFL player and using that false identity to gain the trust of victims. Those are allegations, not proof of guilt, and the legal process will determine the outcome.On the other side, the 49ers have a very real rookie wide receiver wearing No. 7.Whether Stribling chose the number because of personal preference, availability, or any other ordinary reason, one thing is certain: cyberspace has already attached a whole new meaning to it.And that may be the strangest legacy of the Daejon Love saga - not that an alleged fake NFL player became part of football culture, but that his fictional identity continues finding its way into real NFL conversations. articles.title: New NFL Rumors on Aaron Glenn's Potential Jets Hot Seat Ahead of 2026 Season
articles.summary: Despite the New York Jets' poor performance in his first season as head coach, there is reportedly a belief from ownership in what head coach Aaron Glenn is trying to build.
articles.body:
Despite the New York Jets' poor performance in his first season as head coach, there is reportedly a belief from ownership in what head coach Aaron Glenn is trying to build.

According to Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic, any speculation that Jets owner Woody Johnson is already looking for Glenn's replacement is "baseless."

Rosenblatt added that "by all accounts, Johnson is on board with the plan that Glenn and [general manager Darren] Mougey have presented to him."

That plan is reportedly to "build something sustainable," and to not "skip any steps" while doing so.

Johnson and Glenn have a "very close relationship," per Rosenblatt, which suggests Glenn has a chance to keep his job beyond 2026 if the Jets show improvement.

Last season was a rough one for all involved, as the Jets finished 3-14, which was their worst record since a 2-14 mark in 2020.

In addition to tying for the worst record in the league, the Jets ranked 29th in scoring offense and 31st in scoring defense.

Glenn is a former NFL defensive back and defensive coordinator who was expected to at least bring some stability to the Jets' defense, but that was clearly not the case in Year 1.

After firing and replacing a large portion of his coaching staff from last season, Glenn is putting even more on his own plate in 2026, as he will be the defensive play-caller.

That means the bulk of New York's failures and successes on that side of the ball will likely be attributed to him.

The Jets' first test in Year 2 under Glenn will come in Week 1 when the Jets go on the road to face the Tennessee Titans, led by former Jets head coach Robert Saleh, on Sept. 13.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Value Picks to Target After 2026 NFL Roster Cuts
articles.summary: With cutdown day in the rearview, rosters for the 2026 NFL season are nearly set. While many teams will shuffle the deck slightly via the free-agent market over coming days, fantasy managers at least have a clear picture of what depth charts around the league will look like when the campaign kicks off.
articles.body:
With cutdown day in the rearview, rosters for the 2026 NFL season are nearly set. While many teams will shuffle the deck slightly via the free-agent market over coming days, fantasy managers at least have a clear picture of what depth charts around the league will look like when the campaign kicks off.

Shrewd fantasy managers can use these recent roster shakeups to hunt value.

Because squads are limited to just 53 players on the active roster, many backups will see significant action in 2026. While they may not open the year with a fantasy-relevant role, injuries and other unforeseen events could quickly clear a path for these depth options to earn meaningful playing time.

With that in mind, here's a look at five of the best post-cutdown day value picks you can target late in your fantasy draft.

Fantasy points, rankings, average draft position (ADP) and other metrics courtesy of FantasyPros using PPR data.

The discussion around fantasy-relevant Indianapolis Colts running backs has been centered squarely around superstar Jonathan Taylor for the last few seasons, but he may not be the only household name in this backfield by the end of the 2026 campaign.

Seth McGowan, an unheralded rookie seventh-rounder who wasn't even a lock to make the team at the start of the offseason, has surged up the depth chart and is primed to open the year as Taylor's backup. McGowan, Taylor and DJ Giddens—last year's RB2—were the only three backs to stick on Indy's final roster.

McGowan began turning heads early in training camp and continued to thrive throughout the preseason. He put plenty of impressive highlights on tape in practice while cementing himself as the club's No. 2 RB option.

The Athletic's James Boyd said that Taylor would "shoulder the bulk of the workload" for the platoon, but noted McGowan "clearly won the second-string job thanks to his physicality and reliable hands". While 2025 fifth-rounder Giddens will still have a small role after beating out UDFA sophomore Ulysses Bentley IV, McGowan will be the one taking the majority of snaps whenever Taylor rests.

More importantly, McGowan has become the ideal handcuff to snap up late in fantasy drafts. He now has sky-high potential for a feature role should Taylor miss time. While the star back played in all 17 games last year, Taylor has only managed to stay fully healthy twice in six seasons and missed 17 contests between the 2022-24 seasons.

Given the volume that the Colts' coaching staff allocates to the top back in this offense (Taylor has amassed nearly 700 touches over the last two seasons), McGowan would be a borderline fantasy RB1 in any game the starter misses.

Despite this incredible potential, McGowan's is still flying completely under the fantasy radar and only has an ADP of 295 (RB78). This means you'll be able to safely target the rookie in the final round of most drafts.

After being in real danger of being cut by the Pittsburgh Steelers, Kaleb Johnson has found new life as a member of the Green Bay Packers. While it isn't exactly promising to see the 2025 third-rounder get shipped to Titletown for a 2028 sixth-round draft pick, Johnson will have ample opportunity to turn his career following an abysmal start.

The Packers made the move after finding out they would be without their three-time Pro Bowl starting running back indefinitely. Josh Jacobs landed on the Commissioner's Exempt List this weekend, stemming from charges of battery and criminal damage to property after a physical confrontation with his girlfriend. The veteran will not be permitted to practice or attend games while he remains on the exempt list.

Green Bay has opted to forge ahead with three running backs on the active roster. Without Jacobs, the club's platoon consists of incumbents MarShawn Lloyd and Chris Brooks in addition to the recently-acquired Johnson.

While Lloyd is reportedly in line to take the first crack at locking down the starting role during Jacobs' absence, Johnson could still carve out a fantasy-relevant role quickly.

Lloyd has been with the team since he was selected in the third round of the 2024 draft, but only appeared in one game as a rookie and missed all his sophomore season with injuries. Brooks has more experience—he's suited up for 32 games since joining the Packers in 2024—but has only produced 289 yards and one touchdown on 63 totes for the club.

Although Johnson struggled with the Steelers as a rookie (contributing just 69 yards on 28 carries) and still needs to get brought up to speed in a new offense, his potential is undeniable. The 6'1", 224-pound back was a Day 2 pick last year thanks to a rare combination of size, strength, athleticism and finesse, traits that could help him get back on the right track.

For fantasy purposes, consider Johnson a high-upside lottery ticket whose worth stashing at the end of your bench. He may not provide much value right away (which is reflected in his ADP of 220), but injuries or production woes from the players ahead of him on the depth chart will open the door for a breakout.

Odell Beckham Jr. was a longshot to make the New York Giants' final roster after a litany of injuries derailed the past half-decade of his career—including spending 2025 out of football—but the veteran wideout seems rejuvenated by a return to the Big Apple.

With Beckham sticking as one of the five wideouts that new head coach John Harbaugh elected to keep on the 53-man roster, the receiver's much-anticipated comeback could even end up being a meaningful fantasy football storyline.

Beckham hasn't been a reliable fantasy weapon since his stint with the Los Angeles Rams back in 2021. Despite joining the club midway through the campaign, OBJ managed to rate as the WR22 between Weeks 12-18. He went on to miss all of 2022 with injuries before returning to play for Harbaugh's Baltimore Ravens the following year—finishing as the WR63 that season.

Beckham caught on with the Miami Dolphins for the 2024 campaign, but fell off the fantasy radar entirely after tallying just nine catches for 55 yards in nine games for the club. While that showing won't inspire much confidence for his 2026 outlook, the 33-year-old could contribute enough to be worth rostering.

New York has questions within the receiving corps, especially with star wideout Malik Nabers still working his way back to full strength following an ACL tear that limited him to four games in 2025. Joining Beckham as depth options are longtime Big Blue pass-catcher Darius Slayton and a pair of recent additions in veteran Darnell Mooney and rookie Malachi Fields.

The pecking order behind Nabers has yet to be established, but Beckham displayed strong chemistry with quarterback Jaxson Dart throughout the offseason. He even made a few spectacular grabs that had onlookers buzzing:

While Beckham likely won't rekindle the Pro Bowl form of his youth, he enters the year as a projected boom-or-bust injury/bye week fill-in with some flex appeal.

OBJ remains a legitimate deep threat with fantastic hands, giving him the potential to score a touchdown on a weekly basis. That floor, coupled with the upside of an expanded role if players ahead of him on the depth chart are ineffective or injured, make the WR108 with a 341 ADP worth a last-round dice roll in deeper fantasy formats.

The Baltimore Ravens have traditionally leaned heavily on the ground game to generate offense, but the team's passing attack could be its greatest strength in 2026 if rookie wideout Ja'Kobi Lane lives up to the hype he's generated over the past few months.

Lane, a third-round pick out of USC, entered the league as a raw prospect oozing potential. While the 22-year-old only played in 30 games across his three seasons with the Trojans, he tallied 18 touchdown grabs—including 12 during his sophomore campaign alone—and has the talent to translate those scoring chops to the professional level immediately while rounding out the rest of his game with some polish.

It won't be easy for defenders to stop the 6'4", 200-pound receiver, especially one who has the hands and athleticism to turn contested jump balls into easy receptions. He dominated cornerbacks and safeties throughout training camp and the preseason, opening the door for him to begin his career as Baltimore's No. 2 wideout behind established star Zay Flowers.

Lane's contributions this offseason were noticed by teammates, with superstar quarterback Lamar Jackson seeming particularly impressed. Jackson recently had some high praise for the rookie and provided some impressive comps (per Pro Football Talk 's Myles Simmons ):

"Big guy — like 6-4, 6-5 — [he can] catch the ball with the best of them," Jackson said. "I told you, my comparison [is] like Odell Beckham Jr. and DeAndre Hopkins with the hands."

With veteran Rashod Bateman facing potential discipline from the league stemming from his June arrest on family violence charges, Lane could assume an even larger role than initially expected. Fellow rookie Elijah Sarratt and incumbent backups Devontez Walker and LaJohntay Wester are the only other Ravens wideouts to make it through cutdown-day.

Despite his immense potential, Lane is being drafted as the RB61 with an ADP of 174. He's one of the best late-round wideouts you could take right now, offering far more upside than most of his peers found in this range.

The Tennessee Titans are trending towards a breakout campaign in Year 2 of the Cam Ward era. With a new coaching staff taking over and the prized quarterback having another offseason to hone his craft, Tennessee's offense should take a major leap this coming season.

One of the main beneficiaries of this potential improvement will be Gunnar Helm, the unheralded sophomore tight end who is set to play a large part in the team's 2026 plans.

Helm has all the physical tools required to be a prolific pass-catcher. He stands a solid 6'5", 241 pounds and has strong ball skills, talent he flashed as a fourth-round rookie last year. Despite splitting time with entrenched starter Chig Okonkwo and stymied by a listless offense with a porous offense line, Helm still managed to reel in 44 of his 55 targets for 357 yards and two touchdowns.

With Okonkwo departing in free agency, the offensive line getting some much-needed help and a new offensive coordinator in Brian Daboll taking over, you can reasonably expect Helm's fantasy marks to go way up this year. He's the clearcut No. 1 TE on Tennessee's roster, with veteran additions Daniel Bellinger and Kylen Granson likely to log only a handful of targets and mainly stay relegated to blocking duties.

While Helm has the ceiling of a fantasy TE1, he's not even being drafted in most formats. He's currently the TE31 with an ADP of 278, making him a perfect last-round selection and even a preseason free-agent pickup for managers who aren't completely satisfied with the tight ends they came away from their draft with.

His injury helped bring the term " Ammortal chamber " into the lexicon when it was revealed the Rams brought in a futuristic-looking trailer with technology inside that is designed to help stimulate recovery.

Every person in their late-30s and older who has ever experienced back pain immediately tried to find their own chamber after Stafford lit up the NFL by having arguably the best season of his career.

Playing last season at 37 years old, Stafford tied for the third-oldest MVP winner in NFL history. Only Tom Brady (40 in 2017) and Aaron Rodgers (38 in 2021) were older when they won the award.

articles.title: Russell Wilson’s NFL goodbye wasn’t the end of his story as his latest achievements give wife Ciara and fans plenty to celebrate
articles.summary: NFL News: Russell Wilson may have walked away from the NFL, but his life has hardly become quieter. The former quarterback is finding new ways to compete, work .
articles.body: Russell Wilson may have walked away from the NFL, but his life has hardly become quieter. The former quarterback is finding new ways to compete, work and give back. His latest milestone came at Saratoga Race Course, where Club Reign delivered a six-length victory for Wilson and wife Ciara’s new racing venture. The win adds to a busy year that has also included broadcasting, business and continued charitable work.Club Reign’s big Saratoga win gives Russell Wilson and Ciara a memorable start in horse racingWilson and Ciara had a special reason to celebrate on Aug. 29. Their 2-year-old colt, Club Reign, won the first race on the Travers Day card at Saratoga Race Course, giving the couple’s new racing venture an impressive start.Ridden by Edgard Zayas, Club Reign finished six lengths ahead of the field. It was the first-ever race for Three Brand Racing, the ownership group connected to Wilson and Ciara.The moment also had a strong family feel. Ciara was at the track with Wilson and their three children as they celebrated in the winner’s circle. For Wilson, horse racing is not simply another business idea. He has long had an interest in horses, and his brother Harry Wilson helped encourage him to become involved in thoroughbred racing.His family has another connection to the sport. Wilson has spoken about his eldest daughter, Sienna, being an avid horseback rider. That makes the new venture especially meaningful for the family.Club Reign’s performance could also lead to bigger opportunities. The colt is now being considered for major races such as the Grade 1 Champagne Stakes and the Breeders’ Cup Juvenile.Russell Wilson’s move into broadcasting keeps him close to the sport that made him a starAfter 14 seasons in the NFL, Wilson has taken his experience into a new role with CBS Sports. He joined The NFL Today as a studio analyst, giving him a chance to remain involved in football from a different seat.His playing career included a Super Bowl title with the Seattle Seahawks and 10 Pro Bowl selections. He also became the first quarterback in NFL history to reach at least 40,000 passing yards and 5,000 rushing yards.Now, instead of preparing to play on Sundays, Wilson can break down the game and offer insight from the perspective of someone who spent years making those decisions himself.His interests are also moving into areas far removed from the football field. Three Brand Racing, his apparel business and his charitable work are giving him new ways to compete and make an impact.Ciara remains beside Russell Wilson as family, business and philanthropy take center stageCiara has been part of many of Wilson’s biggest moments, including his final stretch in professional football and the family’s celebration at Saratoga.Their latest ventures also show how closely family fits into Wilson’s plans. Three Brand Racing grew from his interest in horses, but it has become something he can share with Ciara and their children.His work with 3BRAND adds another important piece. The company has been connected to contributions toward the Why Not You Foundation, with the total reaching more than $3 million earlier in 2026.Together, these projects paint a picture of a man with plenty to occupy his time after football. Broadcasting keeps him connected to the game, while racing, business and philanthropy allow him to explore interests that were harder to pursue during a demanding NFL career.For Wilson and Ciara, Club Reign’s Saratoga victory was more than a successful afternoon at the track. It was another family milestone and a sign of how much Wilson’s world has expanded since his playing days ended.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: "You have to set expectations with yourself": Why Joe Burrow believes the Bengals’ 2026 Super Bowl push feels ‘inevitable’ after years of frustrating setbacks
articles.summary: NFL News: Joe Burrow does not use the word \"inevitable\" loosely. He used it once before, back in the summer of 2019 at LSU, when something in the building told .
articles.body: Joe Burrow does not use the word "inevitable" loosely. He used it once before, back in the summer of 2019 at LSU, when something in the building told him that team was going to do something special. It did. Fifteen wins, a national championship, and a Heisman Trophy later, that gut feeling had a name. Now, seven years on and sitting in an office off the Bengals' locker room during training camp, Burrow said the word again. Cincinnati, he believes, is built to make a serious run at the Super Bowl in 2026.Why does Joe Burrow think the 2026 Bengals can win the Super Bowl?It starts with the defense, and Joe Burrow is clear about that. The Bengals spent the offseason solving a problem that cost them last season. Defensive line depth was a visible weakness in 2025. This year, they traded up to land Dexter Lawrence II, brought in Jonathan Allen, signed pass rusher Boye Mafe, and added safety Bryan Cook, who arrives with a Super Bowl ring fresh in his memory."The vibe of the defense is really good right now," Burrow said. "Our defensive line is so deep this year. The depth of that unit was a weak point last year. Now we have nine or 10 guys that we feel good about putting out there in five-down sets."That defensive depth changes something important on the offensive side too. For the past couple of seasons, Burrow felt like every possession was desperate, every third down a must-convert situation. That urgency wore on the offense. With a defense capable of keeping games close and manageable, the offense can actually breathe."The last couple of years, it felt like every possession was do or die," he said. "It doesn't really feel that way this year. I think we can commit to the run, we can commit to play-action. We'll drop back and throw it 60 times if we have to, but I don't think that's a recipe for success week in and week out."Coach Zac Taylor has watched the offseason additions change the mood inside the facility. When a player of Burrow's caliber, with his experience and track record, publicly declares a team capable of winning it all, Taylor is not bothered by the pressure that comes with it."Somebody who's been there, done that and knows what it's going to take to get there, we shouldn't shy away from anything he says in that regard," Taylor said.How have Joe Burrow's injuries changed the way he plays Quarterback?Joe Burrow has missed significant playing time in three of his six NFL seasons. A freak wrist injury in 2023, a defense that had aged past its prime in 2024, and turf toe that cost him nine games last year. Each absence left a mark. But each one also taught him something about his own game that he could not have learned staying healthy.Playing through turf toe last season, Burrow lost his mobility. He could not escape pressure the way he normally does. So he adapted, learning to operate from the pocket more efficiently, managing risk earlier in games, and getting rid of the ball to live for the next play."I had to tailor my game to that," he said. "Not being able to move around, I can mitigate risk early in the game until it's needed."That mindset showed up concretely over the final three games of 2025. He completed nearly 77 percent of his passes for 850 yards, nine touchdowns, one interception, and a 125.9 passer rating. The numbers suggest a quarterback who figured something out under the worst conditions.Offensive coordinator Dan Pitcher noticed it too. A late-season checkdown to running back Chase Brown, where Burrow quickly read the defense, abandoned the intended deep route, and delivered a short pass that Brown turned into a 23-yard gain, illustrated the point perfectly."It's just feeling like, if the run game is as good or better than it's ever been and the protections are as good or better than they've ever been, that allows you as the quarterback maybe to not feel like every down is do or die," Pitcher said.Does Joe Burrow think he is the best Quarterback in the NFL right now?Joe Burrow's answer to that question says a lot about how his thinking has matured. He does not chase individual rankings. He smirks at the framing."I always expect to be the best," he said. "The best version of me is going to be the best. I always expect to be the best version of me."When pushed on whether that means best in the league, he pulled back from the label without pulling back from the confidence."I think that's so arbitrary," he said. "Every Sunday, there's going to be a different best player in the league, depending on who you're playing. I really want to win games. I want to be playing when it matters, January, February. That's why you do it."He also has unfinished business at SoFi Stadium specifically. The 2026 Super Bowl returns to the same venue where the Bengals lost to the Rams in February 2022. Burrow's stat line that night was fine. He does not see it that way."I just didn't play good enough," he said. "Not good enough to win a Super Bowl against Matt Stafford. As far as my game now, it's so much more evolved, and I'm such a better player than I was at the time."That is not denial. It is an honest assessment from someone who has studied every layer of what separates good quarterbacks from winning ones in February. And for Burrow, right now, the gap feels smaller than it ever has."I've never understood why people are scared to say it," he said. "You have to set expectations with yourself, your teammates, your organization. Everybody says they want to win the Super Bowl, you talk about it every day, you set that expectation every day, you go and work for it every single day."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Who killed Steve McNair? The chilling story behind the NFL star quarterback’s 2009 murder
articles.summary: NFL News: Trigger Warning: This story contains mention of suicide.Steve McNair’s death remains one of the most distressing tragedies in NFL history.On July 4, 2.
articles.body: Trigger Warning: This story contains mention of suicide.Steve McNair’s death remains one of the most distressing tragedies in NFL history.On July 4, 2009, the former Tennessee Titans and Baltimore Ravens quarterback was found dead inside a Nashville condo alongside his 20-year-old girlfriend, Sahel “Jenni” Kazemi.What initially appeared to be a mysterious “double shooting” was ultimately ruled a “murder-suicide.” But questions surrounding the case have continued to intrigue true crime audiences.So, who killed Steve McNair?The 36-year-old former NFL quarterback Steve McNair had been shot four times: twice in the chest and twice in the head. His 20-year-old girlfriend Sahel Kazemi was found close to his body with a single gunshot wound to the head.A 9mm semiautomatic pistol was recovered near her body. Investigators found no signs of forced entry or a struggle inside the condo.Ballistics evidence and gunshot-residue findings ultimately supported the conclusion that Kazemi was responsible for McNair’s death before taking her own life.Steve McNair and Sahel Kazemi’s relationship ended in tragedyMcNair and Kazemi reportedly dated for several months before their deaths. The retired NFL quarterback was married and had four children, while Kazemi worked as a waitress. According to investigators, tensions had escalated in the days before the shootings.Police said Kazemi was struggling with financial problems and had become disturbed over the possibility that McNair was involved with another woman [another post-marital affair than the one already with her]. Investigators also said she had sent messages suggesting that her life was falling apart and that she was contemplating suicide.“Baby I might have a break down im so stressed,” text was sent from her to him a day before the murder.“Im gonna have all of u soon,” she texted him 24 hours before she shot and killed him and herself.Authorities believed McNair was asleep on the couch when Kazemi shot him. Police said there was no evidence that he had attempted to defend himself in any way.They reconstructed the scene where Kazemi shot McNair four times before positioning herself near him and firing the fatal shot into her own head. Thereby calling it a murder suicide.Why did people continue to question the chilling double murder case?Despite the official ruling, the investigation did not escape scrutiny and controversy.A three-month CBS News investigation later raised questions about the police theory and Kazemi’s state of mind.Investigators discovered extensive communication between Kazemi and 33-year-old Adrian Gilliam Jr., a convicted felon who spent nine years in prison for second-degree murder and attempted armed robbery, and also the man police said sold Kazemi the gun for $100 in a parking lot shortly before the killings.Phone records showed hundreds of calls and texts between the pair during the weeks before McNair’s death, raising questions about whether their relationship was more complicated than initially reported.CBS also reported details that complicated the suggested motive, including a $2,000 transfer from McNair to Kazemi shortly before the killings [to help her pay her bills]. While these revelations fueled speculation, they did not lead authorities to overturn their conclusion.The official answer for Steve McNair’s passingAfter a months-long investigation, Nashville authorities stood by their original conclusion: Sahel Kazemi killed Steve McNair and then died by suicide. Police said they found no evidence that a third person had entered the condo or participated in the killings.McNair’s death abruptly ended the life of a former NFL quarterback remembered for his toughness, leadership, and impeccable football career. Yet the circumstances surrounding his final hours have ensured that his story remains a daunting chapter in sports and true crime.The official answer to: Who killed Steve McNair? is Sahel Kazemi. But the unanswered questions surrounding the investigation are precisely what have kept the case alive in the public imagination more than a decade later. articles.title: Josh Allen Launches Out of Pocket Studios, Will Serve as CEO, Be Executive Producer on All Projects
articles.summary: Buffalo Bills star quarterback Josh Allen is the latest athlete to enter the realm of content production.
articles.body:
Buffalo Bills star quarterback Josh Allen is the latest athlete to enter the realm of content production.

Per Brian Steinberg of Variety , Allen announced the launch of Out of Pocket Studios, which is described as "a media venture that will have him backing entertainment, commercial and experiential projects." The 2024 NFL MVP will serve as CEO of the new company and as an executive producer on all projects.

"Skydance Sports has given me a platform to turn the ideas I care most about into something real," Allen said in a statement. "We're excited to share what Out of Pocket Studios has created so far, and for everyone to see what we're building from here."

The new studio will debut with a TV special called "America's Tailgate," slated to air on CBS on Labor Day. The program will feature music and celebrities and is hosted by NFL Today studio analyst Nate Burleson. Later in the week, "NFL Play Action," a weekly football-analysis studio show hosted by Kyle Brandt and fitness instructor Ally Love, will debut on Paramount+ on Sept. 9.

Other projects from the studio include "The Buffalo Miracle," which "captures the heroism of a McDonald's manager in Buffalo who, during a deadly blizzard in 2022, opened the restaurant to stranded citizens on Christmas Eve." A comedy series conceived by Allen has already been sold and is also on the way.

It will be fun to see how Allen's new endeavor develops, but for now, the star signal-caller will focus on getting ready for the Bills' 2026 season opener against the Houston Texans on Sept. 13.

articles.summary: Eight days from the start of the 2026 NFL season means fantasy managers need to be actively tracking the injury situation for many star players coming out of the preseason.
articles.body:
Eight days from the start of the 2026 NFL season means fantasy managers need to be actively tracking the injury situation for many star players coming out of the preseason.

Among the notable names dealing with injuries going into the regular season are Ja'Marr Chase, Malik Nabers, Jeremiyah Love, Patrick Mahomes, Breece Hall, Mike Evans, George Kittle and Luther Burden.

Here is the latest information on their injuries and most recent update on their potential availability for Week 1.

Chase, who was injured trying to make a catch in practice last week, admitted afterward he could have kept practicing if the situation allowed for it.

The Bengals star is still coming off the board at No. 3 overall in most fantasy drafts, so there's no reason to be concerned about any long-term impact of his knee.

Similarly, albeit coming off a much more significant injury, is Malik Nabers trending toward playing in Week 1. He is being careful about not saying anything definitive , but the fact he has progressed to working with the New York Giants in full practice sessions is a positive sign.

The injury recovery is being factored into where Nabers is going in fantasy drafts. He is currently being drafted as the WR13 and an early third-round pick in 12-team leagues, sandwiched between Rashee Rice and DeVonta Smith.

Mahomes has strongly indicated he is going to play in the season opener, but Kansas City Chiefs head coach Andy Reid is taking a more measured approach in his comments.

There has been nothing from Chiefs camp to suggest Mahomes won't start in Week 1 against the Denver Broncos on Monday Night Football.

One thing that could impact Mahomes' overall fantasy value this year is how often he wants to take off running. He might be reluctant to turn it loose, especially early in the season, as he tests his knee against opposing defenses.

Last season, even with missing the final three games, was Mahomes' best rushing year in the NFL. He finished with 422 yards and five touchdowns on the ground.

Between his knee and the addition of Kenneth Walker III in free agency, Mahomes might not feel the need to run as much. If the Chiefs offense can get back to being anywhere near as explosive as it was earlier in his career, he could be a steal of the draft since he is being drafted as the QB14 and No. 107 player overall.

Jaxson Dart, who has injury issues of his own, is going 13 spots ahead of Mahomes on average.

Emeka Egbuka suffered a toe injury early in training camp, but the Tampa Bay Buccaneers have been optimistic about his Week 1 status since mid-August. Barring something changing in practice this week or next, there's no reason to believe he will be limited in the opener.

Other wide receivers who are expected to play in Week 1 but are lower on the fantasy pecking order include Luther Burden III of the Chicago Bears and Mike Evans of the San Francisco 49ers.

Burden's fantasy hype was reaching borderline absurd levels before he started having groin issues in camp. There are reasons to believe in him having a big 2026, including a Bears offense that looks poised to take another step forward.

Among all receivers with at least 200 routes run last season, Burden's 2.69 yards per route run ranked third behind Puka Nacua (3.70) and Jaxon Smith-Njigba (3.62).

Bears head coach Ben Johnson told reporters after the team's preseason finale that Burden "looks 100 percent to me" in practice.

Evans, despite being on track for Week 1, should be more closely monitored since he has dealt with various lower-body issues throughout camp. His ailments were quad and groin strains that were described as minor.

The 49ers will certainly be hoping that's the case since they are already without Ricky Pearsall for the entire season . Rookie De'Zhaun Stribling has earned high marks throughout training camp and preseason, but if he has to step in right away as the No. 1 target, there figure to be some growing pains along the way.

Evans is being drafted as the WR29 midway through the sixth round. This feels like a safe spot for him because the upside in Kyle Shanahan's offense is huge as long as he stays healthy to play in enough games to make it count.

Sticking with the Niners, George Kittle is expected to practice this week before the team takes off for Australia for the Sept. 10 opener against the Los Angeles Rams.

The 49ers have said they won't rush Kittle back for the opener, but there's a possibility he could play in Week 2 since they don't have to worry about travel for awhile with three straight home games before playing in Seattle on Oct. 11.

Regardless of whether it's Week 1 or Week 2 for Kittle, the fact he is this far in his recovery just eight months after tearing his Achilles in a playoff game is remarkable.

Kittle finished with seven receiving touchdowns in just 11 games and tied for second in fantasy points per game among tight ends last season, so even if he misses time, the upside is high enough that you can bet on him in the middle rounds. Just make sure you have a solid backup option to account for time he could miss.

On the running back front, Jeremiyah Love probably would have been a first-round pick if he were healthy. The Arizona Cardinals made it clear by giving him 14 touches in the preseason game against the Las Vegas Raiders he was going to be a high-volume player.

Unfortunately, the 14th touch is when Love injured his ankle. It was later determined to be a high-ankle sprain, but the Cardinals did not specify what grade of sprain it was.

Typical recovery time for a high ankle sprain ranges from one to six weeks, depending on the severity. Love is going as the RB15 and late in the second round.

NFL Network's Mike Garafolo reported on Tuesday that Love is about "50-50" to play in Week 1.

The Cardinals offense should be interesting from a fantasy perspective because they figure to play a lot of high-scoring games thanks to their defense, but Love's injury makes it hard to fully trust him right out of the gate.

On a more positive note, all indications on Breece Hall are that he will be ready to play in Week 1 after missing time in camp due to a groin injury.

Hall is currently being drafted right behind Love as the RB 16. There's not as much skill position talent on the New York Jets as there is in Arizona, but Geno Smith playing behind a competent offensive line compared to what he had with the Raiders last year offers some upside for the team.

Beyond Hall and Garrett Wilson, there aren't any skill-position players on the Jets who can be trusted yet. Just in terms of volume, Hall is going to be a strong fantasy investment this season.

articles.title: Ex-NFL star Chad Ochocinco dishes his 'storybook' Super Bowl matchup for the 2026 NFL season
articles.summary: Chad Ochocinco wants a Rams-Bengals rematch at SoFi Stadium for Super Bowl LXI, saying Aaron Donald's return makes the Rams almost unbeatable.
articles.body: It’s never too early to think about Super Bowl winners, as we’re just one week away from the 2026 NFL season kicking off. For Chad Ochocinco, he doesn’t want to jump the gun too early on his prediction for Super Bowl LXI before he sees how teams start playing in the regular season. But, if it were up to him, he does have a "storybook" ending to the season he wishes to see happen at SoFi Stadium this upcoming February. And it’s the same Super Bowl matchup the stadium saw the last time it hosted the Super Bowl. CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM "For me, my storybook ending would be a rematch of the 2021 Super Bowl with the Los Angeles Rams and the Cincinnati Bengals again," Ochocinco told OutKick while highlighting his partnership with DraftKings. It was quite the battle between these two teams in 2021, as Matthew Stafford and the Rams, who took a big risk landing the veteran quarterback from the Detroit Lions via trade that offseason, came out on top over Joe Burrow and the Bengals. LOS ANGELES RAMS BETTING OUTLOOK: WHY ONE ANALYST IS ALL IN ON A SUPER BOWL WIN AT +550 Years later, no one could’ve predicted that Stafford would be coming off an MVP 2025 NFL season, and even crazier, Aaron Donald would come out of retirement to join Myles Garrett on the Rams’ defensive line. "Obviously, for Aaron Donald, I love the story. I love the story of him coming out of retirement," Ochocinco said. "I like it when you think about that team defensively and when you think about what they have offensively. They already have a high-powered offense. So, you add Aaron Donald coming back, you already have Myles Garrett. You have [cornerback] Trent McDuffie. "I think everybody would have to get hurt for them to lose. I’m just being honest. It’s almost unfair the kind of team they have right now, it’s the kind of team you build, if you play Madden and you play Ultimate Team, that’s exactly what the Rams are. Offensively and defensively. So, I don’t see them really losing many games. Obviously, you’re going to have some games where you fall short. But I see them coming out of the [NFC} West easily." But Ochocinco’s loyalty lies with his Bengals, the team he spent 10 of his 11 NFL seasons with and continues to believe in today. As someone who never shies away from calling it like it is, Ochocinco loved watching Burrow "being very vocal about not being happy last year and still doing talking this year." Burrow, in a "cryptic format" as Ochocinco put it, made a point to Bengals management that he doesn’t like losing and wants pieces on both sides of the ball to get back to the Super Bowl, which came in just Burrow’s second season in the NFL. The Bengals made sure to extend Burrow’s top receivers, Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, while keeping tight end Mike Gesicki in place as well. Coupled with running back Chase Brown and some fortification on the offensive line, Cincinnati has what it needs on offense, which was never really the question. Could the Bengals’ defense, a pain point for this club for the last couple seasons, get upgrades to match the offensive firepower Zac Taylor’s team possesses? On paper, Ochocinco likes what he sees this time around, to the point where he assumes it’s Super Bowl or bust. "For my Bengals, it’s a put-up-or-shut-up year," he said. "Listen, management has given him everything he needs. You got [Ja’Marr] Chase, you got Tee [Higgins]. They went and did what they needed to do in the offseason, especially defensively. So, he has to get it done. So, I’m assuming this has to be our year. 'WE BACK': AARON DONALD RETURNS TO THE RAMS AND A DEFENSE NOW LOADED WITH MYLES GARRETT AND OTHERS "It’s because Joe Burrow talked about his displeasures publicly in cryptic format. If you’re a player, you understand what he meant. ‘Listen, I take winning serious. Everywhere I’ve been, I’ve always won. The pieces I had around me gave me the opportunity to win, and I want to make sure you guys are aligned with my same core values when it comes to winning and competing and giving me the pieces that I need.’ They showed you offensively and defensively, getting you [defensive tackle] Jonathan Allen, getting Dexter Lawrence, getting [safety Bryan] Cook from Kansas City. We got some good DBs. Therefore, now that you’ve done all the talking, and management has answered your requests, now it’s your turn. It’s on you to stay healthy, stay upright and deliver." Burrow has to stay healthy in Ochocinco’s eyes for the Bengals to get back to the Super Bowl, which seems obvious. However, Burrow’s injury bug struck once again last season, as he played just eight games one season after leading the NFL in passing yards (4,918) and passing touchdowns (43). But then again, is there any team that can take out the Rams this year if they stay healthy? "In a sense it is unfair," Ochocinco said. "But as great as Myles Garrett is, as great as Aaron Donald is, you have to have a scheme. You have to have a plan. You think about a player like Aaron Donald, you’re going to have to double-team somebody. I don’t know who it’s going to be – you’re going to have to pick your poison. Aaron Donald, the last time he played, he had a 20-sack season and he was double-teamed 64% of the team. And still had 20 sacks – that’s unheard of. Then, you have Myles Garrett coming off a 23-sack season. So, I mean, what do you do? When you have players like that come upfield so hard, I’m thinking about quick game. The ball has to come out quick, so they don’t have the time to be able to get to the quarterback. Also, running the ball, I think misdirection. You got to get them going one way and get them to stop their feet because they’re so good. It’s easy for me say what you need to do. It’s another thing to go out there and execute it in a structured environment. I’m not sure, but they have their hands full." OCHO LOVES DRAFTKINGS GAMEDAY We’ll see how the 17-game-plus season shakes out, but discussions and predictions like these with Ochocinco prove that football is back, and he’s excited to impact the fan experience with DraftKings. "DraftKings Gameday," which will take place on Sept. 2, was announced on Monday with quite the activation as it celebrates the first football season with DraftKings Sports & Casino available in all 50 states. As a way to fuel fans with the return of football, DraftKings will be offering free gas, while supplies last, to passenger vehicles at select gas stations in Los Angeles, Miami, Dallas, Atlanta and Detroit. Specific locations and event times will be announced separately. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "For me, I think it’s fun because who else would do something like this outside of DraftKings. This is a great touch for NFL fans to start the season," Ochocinco said. "We’re giving you free gas, so when your respective team plays, you’re fueled up to go. And word of mouth will be, ‘You won’t believe this? You know what DraftKings did? I was able to save money and get tickets to go to a game because they paid for my gas.’ That makes sense." There will also be exclusive DraftKings Gameday promotions for customers, a customized in-app experience, in-person activations, a charitable donation through the DraftKings SERVES program, and a new campaign featuring Kevin Hart and Nick Jonas this season. "It’s all about the fan experience, so some of the offers and luxuries throughout the season is what sets us apart from everybody else. I’m happy to be a part of them," Ochocinco said.

articles.title: "If the wife wasn’t happy, it wasn’t going to get done": How the real story behind Aaron Donald's stunning NFL return has almost nothing to do with football
articles.summary: NFL News: Aaron Donald is back. The three-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year has ended his retirement, signing a one-year, $20 million deal with the Los Ange.
articles.body: Aaron Donald is back. The three-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year has ended his retirement, signing a one-year, $20 million deal with the Los Angeles Rams more than two years after walking away from the game. The announcement on August 30 sent the football world into a frenzy. But once Donald stood at the podium and started talking, it became clear fast that the biggest factor in his return was not Myles Garrett or Sean McVay. It was his wife, Erica.What role did Erica Donald play in Aaron Donald's NFL comeback?Aaron Donald was candid about it at his press conference. He said he was genuinely unsure whether he wanted to return, and that the decision only moved forward once his household was on board. "If the wife wasn't happy, it wasn't going to get done. I got to make sure that the household was good, the kids were okay with it all," he said.That is not the kind of quote you usually get from a player announcing a comeback. Athletes tend to talk about competitive drive, unfinished business, or a hunger that never left. Donald skipped all of that and went straight to the truth. His family had to come first.He described days when he wavered, saying, "I don't know," and it was Erica who steadied him. "She talked to me enough to be like, 'You want to do this. Don't make no decisions faster than what you need to make a decision. Take your time,'" he said. That kind of patience is easy to underestimate. Erica was not pushing him toward a decision. She was making sure he arrived at the right one.Donald put it simply: "My wife was on board. She said, 'If you want to do this, (I'm) with (you) 100%.'" He added that she played a "huge part" in helping him figure it out, calling it "a lot of hard work, a lot of long conversations."Two years away from football changes a man. Donald had built something at home, a routine, a presence, a life that did not revolve around training camps and game weeks. Going back meant disrupting all of that. The fact that Erica not only agreed but actively encouraged him says something about how much she understood what this meant to him, even when he could not fully articulate it himself.What did Erica Donald post after Aaron Donald's comeback was announced?Shortly after the news became official, Erica took to X with just seven words: "I let him out the house y'all." It landed perfectly. Funny, warm, and with just enough truth behind it to make it stick.ESPN's Adam Schefter reposted her message and wrote, "One of the primary reasons Aaron Donald has returned." Former Rams cornerback Jalen Ramsey replied calling her "the real MVP." The post racked up tens of thousands of likes within hours.What made it work was the contrast. While analysts broke down the Rams' defensive scheme and debated Donald's conditioning at 34, Erica reduced the whole saga to a household joke. And she was not wrong. The most consequential conversation in this comeback did not happen in a team facility. It happened at home, over multiple nights, between a husband who was not sure and a wife who helped him get there.Donald is returning to chase something football has left unfinished. But behind every great athlete making a decision this size, there is usually someone who made it possible. In this case, she said it herself.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Stupidest S--t I've Ever Heard,' Colts GM Chris Ballard Blasts Idea of NFL Players Returning to CFB
articles.summary: Indianapolis Colts general manager Chris Ballard has weighed in on the ongoing debate around players who were signed to NFL contracts being allowed to return to play in college.
articles.body:
Indianapolis Colts general manager Chris Ballard has weighed in on the ongoing debate around players who were signed to NFL contracts being allowed to return to play in college.

Speaking to reporters on Tuesday, Ballard called it the "stupidest s--t I've ever heard" when addressing the topic.

The situation really picked up steam in mid-August when a federal judge granted a temporary restraining order allowing a group of former college players to enter the transfer portal even though some were on NFL rosters.

That led to LSU signing Dae'Quan Wright, who spent the summer with the Philadelphia Eagles and Cleveland Browns after going undrafted in the 2026 NFL draft. He was waived by the Browns last week.

Wright played the past two seasons for head coach Lane Kiffin at Mississippi. Kiffin is entering his first year at LSU.

Multiple conferences, including the SEC , Big Ten and ACC , followed up by passing rule changes preventing players who have signed contracts with a pro team from being able to return to college to play for a team in their conference.

However, a Dallas-based judge signed an order on Aug. 27 prohibiting the NCAA, SEC and SEC commissioner Greg Sankey from preventing a group of athletes from returning to college for another season.

There were a total of 41 players on the order, several who played football but also Christeen Iwuala and Bailey Maupin after they signed WNBA contracts earlier in the summer.

Kiffin told reporters on Monday that LSU's leadership committee, comprised of several players on the football team, were "emphatic" in their enthusiasm about the program adding former pro players if it helps them win games.

LSU is still waiting for official guidance from court orders and the SEC before making any final decisions about whether or not the players will participate in games, but Kiffin did say he will "absolutely follow" whatever the decision ends up being.

articles.title: Colin Kaepernick won't support NFL, says league is 'actively blackballing me' and others who protested
articles.summary: Colin Kaepernick still watches football, just not the NFL.
articles.body:
It's been 10 years since San Francisco 49ers quarterback Colin Kaepernick took a knee during the national anthem as a way to protest what he perceived as oppression against Black people and people of color in the United States.

"I am not going to stand up to show pride in a flag for a country that oppresses Black people and people of color," Kaepernick explained 10 years ago. "To me, this is bigger than football and it would be selfish on my part to look the other way. There are bodies in the street and people getting paid leave and getting away with murder."

Kaepernick, who has not played in the NFL since 2016 gave a rare interview with NBC News in which he discussed his protest and the effects of it.

In the interview, Kaepernick said he hasn't watched an NFL game since he was exiled from the league following the 2016 NFL season. He also made it clear that he believes the league is still " blackballing " him and targeting others who protested.

"I'm not gonna support an organization that one, is actively blackballing me, but two, has targeted my brothers who have been protesting as part of this as well," Kaepernick says. "I watch college football."

During the interview, Kaepernick discussed the origin of the kneeling and whether it had support from military veterans. Kaepernick said it was teammate Eric Reid — who took a knee with Kaepernick on Sept. 1, 2016 — who suggested the gesture as a form of protest.

At the time, it was suggested that a former Green Beret, Nate Boyer, came up with the idea for Kaepernick and Reid to take a knee, but that wasn't actually the case. Boyer did meet with both players, with Kaepernick asking how he could protest without angering those in the military. Boyer said people would be angry no matter what, adding that sitting on the bench — which Kaepernick was doing during the national anthem prior to Sept. 1 — was not an inspiring way to get their message across.

Boyer then told Kaepernick he believed sitting on the bench "wasn't the most inspiring" and that the protest could be more effective if he was next to his teammates, perhaps bowing his head while standing. "He said no immediately, and I respect that," Boyer says, and the conversation then logically turned to taking a knee. He doesn't dispute that the two players may have come to that conclusion before meeting him.

Boyer then told Kaepernick he believed sitting on the bench "wasn't the most inspiring" and that the protest could be more effective if he was next to his teammates, perhaps bowing his head while standing.

"He said no immediately, and I respect that," Boyer says, and the conversation then logically turned to taking a knee. He doesn't dispute that the two players may have come to that conclusion before meeting him.

After the game, Reid claimed Boyer was on board with the idea. Kaepernick said he didn't dispute that at the time because he didn't want the conversation to devolve into a "back-and-forth."

Kaepernick's decision to kneel caused a significant reaction both inside and outside the NFL. Within the game, a player group chat reportedly grew contentious, with then-Seattle Seahawks cornerback Richard Sherman reportedly telling Kaepernick he "shouldn't tell players how to protest," per NBC News.

Outside the game, Kaepernick became a popular political lightning rod. Then-Supreme Court Justice Ruth Bader Ginsburg said Kaepernick's protest was "dumb and disrespectful," though she later apologized for her remarks. Before his first presidential term, Donald Trump famously said he wished owners would say, " Get that son of a bitch off the field right now, out, he's fired. He's fired!" when players protested.

On top of that, angry fans burned Kaepernick's jersey.

Kaepernick said the criticism he faced for taking a knee was a way to distract from the actual message he was trying to send, per NBC News.

"The critique of the method is a way to distract from the actual message," Kaepernick says. "The conversation that was being had is taking a knee is more problematic than Black people being killed. Just simply put, 'Hey, we need to talk about taking a knee. This is urgent. We need to resolve this.' But another Black person gets killed, and it's like, 'Oh well, that's kind of normal.'"

Despite all of that, Kaepernick spent the 2016 NFL season with the 49ers. While he did not open the year as the team's starter — losing that role to Blaine Gabbert — Kaepernick eventually came off the bench to start 11 games down the stretch.

He finished the season with 16 passing touchdowns and four interceptions.

At the end of the season, the 49ers told Kaepernick he would be released. Despite leading the team to the Super Bowl in 2012 and reaching the AFC conference championship in 2013, Kaepernick met with just one team during the 2017 offseason — the Seahawks.

Kaepernick said other coaches — like then-Baltimore Ravens coach John Harbaugh — expressed interest in signing him, but were shut down by those above them.

In 2017, Kaepernick eventually filed a grievance against the league, alleging collusion to keep him out of the NFL. He settled with the league in 2019.

In the years since his decision to kneel, Kaepernick made it clear he wanted to return to the NFL. Despite repeatedly saying he was ready to come back, Kaepernick remained unsigned.

Throughout that entire saga, NFL commissioner Roger Goodell has denied collusion by the league, saying teams are free to make their own decisions when it comes to personnel.

In the years since his NFL exit, Kaepernick has continued his work as an activist, winning a number of awards for his ability to make an impact. He's also published a children's book and been the subject of a Netflix series.
