articles.title: Fresh Fantasy Football 2026 Funny League Names to Entertain Your Friends
articles.summary: The simplest-sounding decisions aren't always made the quickest.
articles.body:
The simplest-sounding decisions aren't always made the quickest.

If you are, for instance, tasked with naming a fantasy football league ahead of the 2026 NFL season, maybe you've left this as one of the final items on your to-do list. And maybe you're hoping inspiration will be spurred by the approaching of the upcoming opening kick, and that everything will magically fall into place right when it needs to.

Or maybe you've already realized there's a flaw in that plan, which is how you wound up here. You might be scrambling for any solution at the moment, battling a rare form of writer's block. Luckily, we're help to ease that anxiety and tilt this fight in your favor with a breakdown of different naming ideas to guide you through this more-complicated-than-it-sounds process.

While you can go a bunch of different directions with your league name, you don't want that abundance to feel overwhelming. There can, in fact, be too much of a good thing, and sometimes it leaves you stuck feeling analysis paralysis.

If you're at all fearing that kind of outcome, the simplest solution for you might be the most obvious one. It's a first-thought, best-thought kind of deal.

You don't have to go the generic route, but it might be the easiest choice, especially if you don't know a lot (or any) of your leaguemates. If you want to keep the focus on football, then something as easy as "Any Given Sunday" or "Monday Morning Quarterbacks" might work. Granted, the creativity is lacking, but maybe that's OK.

And this doesn't have to be so bland. Maybe there's a simple bond you all share that could make the choice of obvious, like a graduating class year if that's what brought you all together or something location-specific if you're all nearby.

The simple route won't be the best for everyone. If you double as fantasy commisioner and resident life of the party, you'll want something more entertaining.

This is where the fun starts. While you could tie things toward popular culture (an option we'll examine later), you don't have to exit the sports world to have some fun. If you're all NFL diehards, why not build the league title around that?

If you're all members of the same fanbase, then put that into play. Maybe you're the "Lambeau Leapers" if you're all Green Bay Packers backers or the "YAC Bros" if you all root for the San Francisco 49ers.

If you want to get punny, then pulling something from pop culture is almost always the right idea. There's just an almost endless amount of material to work with, and this can be where your creativity stretches the farthest.

If any TV shows or movies unite the league members, then that should narrow your focus pretty quick.

Or if you all share music tastes, then let that be your guide.

Clearly, you have options, but only you know which will work best for you and your league mates.

articles.title: Odell Beckham Jr.'s New Giants Jersey Number Revealed in Video Ahead of 2026 NFL Season
articles.summary: Odell Beckham Jr. is back in the jersey in which he started out his NFL career.
articles.body:
Odell Beckham Jr. is back in the jersey in which he started out his NFL career.

The New York Giants wide receiver will wear No. 13 after making the cut for the 53-man roster, his team announced Tuesday.

Beckham originally wore No. 3 after signing with the Giants earlier this offseason.

Wide receiver Jalin Hyatt has worn No. 13 for the Giants since 2023. Hyatt was waived Sunday and re-signed to the team's practice squad.

Beckham wore No. 13 from 2014 to 2018 with the Giants while starting out his career with three straight Pro Bowl seasons and an Offensive Rookie of the Year campaign.

He also wore No. 13 with the Cleveland Browns from 2019 to 2021 before switching to No. 3 after a midseason trade to the Los Angeles Rams.

Hyatt was drafted by the Giants in 2023, at which point Beckham publicly approved of him wearing No. 13.

Beckham has since worn No. 3 for the Baltimore Ravens and Miami Dolphins, the latter of which released the veteran wideout in December 2024. Beckham has yet to see regular-season NFL action since.

The wide receiver said after successfully making the Giants roster he would be speaking with Hyatt about switching back.

"I think we all know what that means to me," Beckham said Monday about the No. 13 jersey . "There will definitely be some conversations. I'll just say, we'll see what happens, but like I said, it would be an honor and a privilege to put that back on."

Beckham is set to make his NFL comeback and his first appearance for the Giants since 2018 when his team opens the campaign Sunday, Sept. 13 against the visiting Dallas Cowboys.

He isn't the only player getting a new jersey after rosters were finalized Sunday. Rookie wide receiver Malachi Fields is going from No. to No. 88, per North Jersey's Art Stapleton.

articles.title: Tony Romo Issues Statement After Being Placed on Indefinite Leave from CBS
articles.summary: Tony Romo has issued a statement in the wake of CBS placing him on indefinite leave.
articles.body:
Tony Romo has issued a statement in the wake of CBS placing him on indefinite leave.

In the statement released online, Romo took responsibility for what he described as his "failures" that led to his leave from the network he has worked for as part of its NFL coverage since 2017.

Romo also noted in the statement he pleaded "no contest to a civil offense for OWI in Wisconsin" on Tuesday.

CBS Sports is elevating J.J. Watt as part of its lead broadcast team, alongside play-by-play man Jim Nantz and sideline reporter Tracy Wolfson for the start of the 2026 NFL season.

Watt joined CBS in 2023 as a studio analyst before joining the broadcast team as part of the No. 2 crew prior to the start of last season. His first game with Nantz will be on Sept. 13 for the Green Bay Packers-Minnesota Vikings matchup.

Romo went right from the NFL to the broadcast booth. He announced his retirement after 13 seasons with the Dallas Cowboys in April 2017, then signed with CBS Sports as the lead game analyst.

In his second season in the booth, Romo was on the call for Super Bowl 53 between the New England Patriots and Los Angeles Rams. The Patriots won 13-3 in what turned out to be Tom Brady's final championship with the franchise.

Romo has been on the call for three Super Bowls, including Brady's final win during the 2020 season with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and the second matchup between the Kansas City Chiefs and San Francisco 49ers in February 2024.

articles.body:
Former Dallas Cowboys quarterback and current CBS Sports NFL analyst Tony Romo released a statement on Tuesday saying that multiple back surgeries during his 14-year career led him down a road toward a dependence on pain medication and and "over-reliance" on alcohol.

The statement from Romo comes after he plead no contest on Tuesday to operating while intoxicated after being arrested by the Milwaukee County Sheriff's Office in July .

Romo stressed in his statement that he wasn't making excuses for his actions and that he takes full responsibility for the situation. He added that he is working with doctors to address his health and that he is grateful for the support he's received from people around the NFL.

"Football has shaped nearly every meaningful part of my life. I played for more then 20 years, including 14 in the NFL with the Dallas Cowboys. After my retirement, CBS gave me the profound honor of staying close to the game through broadcasting. "Playing taught me the power of relationships, the strength of a team, and the toughness to face failure head-on with honesty, resilience, and the determination to do better. "This is one of those moments when I am leaning on everything football taught me. "This morning, I faced a recent personal failure by pleading no contest to a civil offense for OWI in Wisconsin. I own this completely. "Multiple back surgeries ended by career earlier than I expected and left me with constant, debilitating pain. That pain led to a dependence on pain medication, and my efforts to get off those medications led to an over-reliance on alcohol. "As I have taught my three young sons: when you fall short, you stand up and take full responsibility. That is an important first step. The harder and more important step is examining the path that brought you here and making the changes necessary to move forward. "That path requires honesty. "None of this is an excuse. These are my failures, and I take responsibility for them. "The past month has been difficult, but it had also been personally significant. It has required me to confront and own my mistakes fully — to the Lord, to myself, to my family, and now to the public. "I am working closely with a team of doctors to address my health and make the necessary changes. I am deeply grateful for the support of my family, my friends, and the NFL community including players, coaches, and owners. Your encouragement has meant more than you know. "As I turn my attention to my health, my family, and, in time, my return to CBS, I kindly ask for privacy during this period."

articles.title: The 5 biggest takeaways from the Chiefs’ 53-man roster reveal
articles.summary: Here are the most important notes from Kansas City’s initial roster for the 2026 season.
articles.body:
The dust is still settling on the chaos of NFL cutdown day, when the Kansas City Chiefs and 31 other NFL teams must cut down 90-man rosters to 53 players to begin the season.

The Chiefs' initial 53-man roster was announced on Sunday evening and has been adjusted a couple of times since. The practice squad is still being finalized , with the season's opening game now under two weeks away.

We've had time to digest the moves Kansas City made, so let's sort out the top takeaways:

1. The Chiefs have one of the NFL's youngest rosters

According to Bill Speros of Bookies.com , the Chiefs' initial 53-man roster was the third-youngest in the NFL. That was the case before the team waived two second-year players in favor of two rookies.

Arrowhead Pride user Dandridge pointed this out in The Feed on Sunday evening :

The biggest standout to me is Andy going against form and relying so heavily on youthful, inexperienced, potential for depth instead of proven, low-ceiling veterans.

On the flip side, AFC West foes like the Denver Broncos and Los Angeles Chargers rank among the top 7 oldest rosters.

The Chiefs will be looking to reclaim the throne in the division with the youngest roster of the bunch.

2. The Chiefs' backfield could be a one-two punch

One of the most surprising cuts of the weekend was the Chiefs' decision to waive veteran running back Emari Demercado, who was claimed by the Dallas Cowboys on the waiver wire.

This is notable because of Demercado's experience compared to the backups behind lead running back Kenneth Walker. Earlier in the offseason, Demercado told local media that pass blocking was his niche in the NFL, and Kansas City — with a heightened sense of protecting quarterback Patrick Mahomes — was willing to let that go.

It speaks to the trust in rookie running back Emmett Johnson and second-year back Brashard Smith, especially Johnson. To my eye, Smith has improved on the fundamentals of the position, but he still lacks the strength to run between the tackles and pick up pass rushers one-on-one consistently throughout a game.

On the other hand, Johnson is a natural running back in all facets and has proven it in the preseason. There's a chance Walker and Johnson are splitting the majority of the work, whether it's a run or pass play, and Smith plays less often as a change-of-pace back in the third-wheel position.

Disappointed in Pole — more disappointed in his performance this preseason than in his not making the team. Was expecting him to take a significant step forward this year, but just didn't seem to happen.

When the Chiefs traded for Baltimore Ravens rookie left tackle Diego Pounds last week, alarm bells went off in Chiefs Kingdom about that position. Local media quieted the concerns about left tackle Josh Simmons' (Back) situation being related to the move.

It turns out that second-year left tackle Esa Pole had just overstayed his welcome. On Sunday, he was cut for the second straight preseason; he elected to join the Washington Commanders ' practice squad rather than returning to Kansas City.

Some players are gamers, showing up when the lights are on but not meeting that performance level in practice. Pole filled in admirably last season on the blind side, but it's clear the team was not impressed with how he built on that this offseason.

One of the most polarizing moves of the weekend was the Chiefs' roster maneuvering at the bottom of the receiver depth chart. With six players in the group, starting kick and punt returner Nikko Remigio beat out second-year wideout Andrew Armstrong for the last spot. Armstrong cleared waivers and returned to Kansas City's practice squad on Monday.

So it's a happy ending (for now) for both sides of the discussion surrounding the roster battle. User Mikek1989 put it best in The Feed :

The fact the majority of people are going to complain about our WR6-7 battle speaks about where this team is. KC is freakin BACK BABY!!

The fact the majority of people are going to complain about our WR6-7 battle speaks about where this team is.

To my eye, Armstrong put together a strong enough camp to warrant a roster spot, but that's why I'm just a blogger. General manager Brett Veach knew he would retain Armstrong, giving the team a quality depth option should the Chiefs need to call up the 6-foot-4 receiver who built chemistry with Mahomes during training camp due to injuries at the position.

It's also worth noting that both wide receivers Jalen Royals and rookie Cyrus Allen have shown enough to feel confident in as backups to the projected starting three. If either or both had not impressed, Armstrong might have been a stronger consideration to keep.

This may be the best draft class I've seen for the Chiefs–ever.

Kansas City currently has 11 rookies on the roster:

Yes, over one-fifth of the Chiefs are first-year players, which alludes to the first bullet point of this list. This team isn't just going young; it's relying on many first-year players to fill out the team's depth. It speaks to the exciting, long-term prospects of the roster — but also the fragility of the team in 2026. Kansas City doesn't have the reliable veterans on the fringes of the team to fall back on for the "next-man-up mentality."

It remains to be seen whether that is a positive or negative change to a long-time trend for the Chiefs under head coach Andy Reid and defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo.

articles.title: Falcons named among NFL's biggest preseason losers
articles.summary: CBS Sports includes Atlanta on its list of preseason losers
articles.body:
The Atlanta Falcons are finished with an odd but telling preseason schedule. They whooped on an awful Indianapolis Colts defense and outlasted the backups for the Miami Dolphins . They also got soundly beaten by the only good team they faced: taking a 27-7 loss when they played the Denver Broncos , who may be the favorites in the AFC.

The Falcons' quarterback situation looks no better now than it was at the start of last month, and for a cherry on top they've lost 1.5 of their best pass rushers for the season.

It should come as no surprise then that Atlanta has been included on CBS Sports' list of the NFL's biggest losers of the 2026 preseason.

"After an awful preseason debut with the Falcons, Tua Tagovailoa was much better in Week 3 ... - The Falcons haven't had much of an opportunity to remove him from QB1 status, though. Michael Penix Jr. only recently returned to full team drills, and he didn't play in the preseason finale... Add in Jalon Walker's torn ACL and James Pearce Jr.'s eight-game suspension, and it was a rough preseason ahead of what could be a rough regular season."

If there's a silver lining, it's that the bar for the Falcons is about as low as it gets in the NFL.

On paper, the NFC South is still the weakest division in the league, and the Carolina Panthers won it last season despite a -69 scoring differential.

The New Orleans Saints are a popular pick to go from worst to first, but we're unimpressed by an aging roster outside of second-year quarterback Tyler Shough and rookie wideout Jordyn Tyson, who will begin the season on injured reserve.

The Panthers will be facing a far more-difficult schedule thanks to their division "win" and they've been hit hard by injuries this month, including season-ending knee issues for wide receiver Chris Brazzell II and edge rusher Nic Scourton. They are also missing their starting offensive tackles.

The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have dominated this division in recent years but they also face an aging roster and they no longer have Mike Evans around to bully their rivals twice a year.

A healthy Falcons team is still the most-talented in this group - if they can manage to get to Week 9 without falling out of the boat they should have a fighting chance to win their first division title since 2017.

articles.title: Packers GM Brian Gutekunst Denies Josh Sweat, Cardinals Trade Buzz With Blunt Statement
articles.summary: Green Bay Packers general manager Brian Gutekunst emphatically shot down a recent trade rumor that linked his team to Arizona Cardinals defensive end Josh Sweat.
articles.body:
Green Bay Packers general manager Brian Gutekunst emphatically shot down a recent trade rumor that linked his team to Arizona Cardinals defensive end Josh Sweat.

Per ESPN's Rob Demovsky , Gutekunst told reporters on Tuesday that the Packers and Cardinals haven't had any trade discussions involving the former Pro Bowler.

"Somebody's making stuff up," Gutekunst said bluntly.

Sweat is under contract with the Cardinals through the 2028 season, but he would be an obvious fit with the Packers. After starting his career with the Philadelphia Eagles, he followed defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon to Arizona after he became the team's head coach and produced a career-high 12 sacks in 2025.

Gannon is now Green Bay's defensive coordinator, fueling the expectation that the team would pursue Sweat as a replacement for star edge rusher Micah Parsons, who will start the 2026 campaign on the PUP list.

The Packers only kept four edge rushers on their initial 53-man roster in Lukas Van Ness, Barryn Sorrell, Brenton Cox Jr. and rookie Dani Dennis-Sutton, so they could use some extra depth. For now, it sounds like Sweat isn't on Gutekunst's wishlist as the start of the 2026 season approaches.

articles.title: NFL Insider Hypes Baker Mayfield as 'Top-10' QB, Predicts 'Big Season' Amid Bucs Contract Dispute
articles.summary: Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield is betting on himself as he enters the final year of his contract, and some around the NFL expect him to deliver in a big way in 2026.
articles.body:
Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield is betting on himself as he enters the final year of his contract, and some around the NFL expect him to deliver in a big way in 2026.

ESPN's Jeremy Fowler spoke to an NFL personnel evaluator who said they feel Mayfield is poised for a bounce-back year during the upcoming campaign.

"When he's healthy, he's a top-10 quarterback," the exec said. "I don't think he was healthy last year. He should have a big season."

After throwing for career highs of 4,500 yards and 41 touchdowns in 2024, Mayfield's numbers dropped to 3,693 yards and 26 touchdowns last season as the Bucs fell short of the playoffs for the first time since 2019. The 31-year-old turned down a reported two-year extension offer worth over $100 million because he feels he deserves more long-term security in Tampa Bay.

It's clear that Mayfield will be playing the 2026 season with a chip on his shoulder, so he could be set to prove his doubters wrong. The Bucs will open the year against the Cincinnati Bengals on Sept. 13.

articles.title: Tony Romo guilty of OWI in Milwaukee, will have license revoked for 6 months
articles.summary: Former Dallas Cowboys quarterback and CBS NFL analyst Tony Romo Sept. 1 pleaded no contest to an OWI citation tied to his July 23 arrest in Milwaukee.
articles.body:
Former Dallas Cowboys quarterback and CBS NFL analyst Tony Romo on Tuesday, Sept. 1, pleaded no contest to an operating while intoxicated citation tied to his late July arrest in Milwaukee and will have his driving privileges revoked for six months.

Three other pending forfeitures against Romo were dismissed, online court records show. Romo's plea comes just days after a spokesperson for him told the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel and other media outlets that Romo "accepts full responsibility for his actions."

In addition to having his license suspended for six months, Romo must pay a $748 fine by Nov. 2.

The Milwaukee County Sheriff's Office arrested Romo July 23 after a deputy pulled him over on southbound Interstate 43 and he performed poorly on a field sobriety test . Romo, a Burlington native, was in the area to participate in the Wisconsin Amateur Championship golf event in West Bend and told the deputy that he was driving to a family member's house after the event concluded.

Police originally cited Romo for refusing to take an intoxication test after his arrest . On Aug. 27, he received additional citations for first-offense operating while intoxicated , unsafe passing on the right side and possessing open intoxicants in his vehicle.

Following his arrest, CBS placed Romo on leave until further notice.

articles.title: Much of the Eagles' Super Bowl LIX core remains intact
articles.summary: Despite the expected constant roster turnover, the Eagles continue preserving the foundation of a championship contender.
articles.body:
Every NFL offseason brings predictions about the end of a contender's run. Star players leave, contracts become expensive, and eventually the roster that reached the mountaintop begins to look very different than the one that hoisted a Lombardi Trophy. The Philadelphia Eagles know that well, not being even two years removed from their most recent Super Bowl win. Add to that they they have experienced plenty of that change over the past two years.

Sure, much of the roster is familiar, but as is the case with every NFL squad, known names have departed. New faces have arrived. Still, after unveiling their initial 53-man roster , one reality remains clear. Much of the foundation that helped deliver a championship is still in place.

According to roster data compiled following Sunday's cutdown deadline, 14 of the 22 starters from Philadelphia's Super Bowl-winning team remain on the roster. Eight offensive starters are still in the building, while six defensive starters continue anchoring Vic Fangio's unit.

Maintaining continuity while constantly refreshing a roster is one of the NFL's most difficult balancing acts. General manager Howie Roseman has built a reputation for making difficult decisions before sentiment can interfere with long-term planning.

Howie Roseman continues walking a difficult line

The latest roster snapshot shows Roseman isn't simply tearing down and rebuilding every offseason . The Eagles still feature cornerstone players such as Jalen Hurts, Saquon Barkley, DeVonta Smith, Dallas Goedert, Lane Johnson, Jordan Mailata, Landon Dickerson, Cam Jurgens, Jalen Carter, Quinyon Mitchell and Cooper DeJean.

Those players form the backbone of a roster that still carries championship expectations entering 2026, despite the Los Angeles Rams' efforts . The continuity extends beyond the starting lineup. Jake Elliott remains with the organization as one of only two remaining players from the Eagles' Super Bowl LII championship team (Lane Johnson is the other). Elliott's presence serves as a reminder of how much has changed, but it also highlights the consistency Philadelphia has maintained throughout multiple roster cycles.

14 of the Eagles' expected 22 starters from Super Bowl LIX are still on the roster. In an era defined by salary-cap casualties, free-agent departures, and constant roster churn, that's a significant number.

Roseman has spent years proving that sustaining success requires more than simply keeping everyone together. It requires identifying which players are foundational, replacing the pieces that leave, and resisting the temptation to cling to the past for sentimental reasons. The Eagles have lost talent since hoisting the Lombardi Trophy, but their initial 53-man roster suggests the organization's championship blueprint remains largely intact.

Whether that foundation is strong enough to support another title run will be determined over the coming months. For now, however, Philadelphia enters the 2026 season looking less like a team trying to recapture what it once had and more like one still building from it.

articles.title: This Olympian battled porn addiction for years. He now wants to help others suffering in silence
articles.summary: Like almost every boy, Freddie Woodward was exposed to porn at an early age.
articles.body: Like almost every boy, Freddie Woodward was exposed to porn at an early age. At first, it was nothing more than a glance at adult magazines or material shared between friends. Then, as he got older, he stepped into the seemingly endless world of online videos, which offered a quick hit of dopamine for a curious mind. If we put embarrassment aside, his relationship with adult content was nothing out of the ordinary; it’s a familiar path followed by millions of people worldwide. Woodward continued watching porn during a childhood spent excelling in sport. He was spotted as a potential talent while at school and put on a pathway to becoming a professional diver. The goal was reaching the 2016 Olympic Games in Rio. “I always say diving found me; I didn’t find diving,” he told CNN Sports. “Immediately, I was in this elite pathway. It was never recreational diving. From the get-go, we’re trying to make Olympic athletes from this and so it was four, five, six days a week almost immediately.” The talent was obviously there, but Woodward admits he never truly believed he would make the Olympic squad because he was growing up in a golden generation of British divers – including the likes of Olympic champion Tom Daley. But through dedication, sacrifice and an obsessive work ethic, Woodward secured the last spot on Team GB in 2016, where he went on to finish 19th in the springboard diving event. “It was an insane feeling, and in a sense, I wasn’t there with medal-winning expectations, so while it felt like such a big deal for me, there was a bit of pressure off.” But while he excelled on the sporting stage, Woodward had continued to fall deeper into the world of online porn. It wasn’t as if he was living a dramatic double life – where he would race home from training and spend countless hours in front of the laptop – his relationship with adult content was more insidious than that. It was so subtle that he didn’t necessarily realize, or at least admit to himself, that something was wrong. Although watching porn became an almost daily occurrence, Woodward was still out socializing, dating and living an otherwise fulfilling life. But, looking back now, he can see how his habit was starting to corrode different areas of his life. “I first had these little niggles about it as a slightly older teenager trying to go through exams,” he said. “Any time I came to do any sort of revision, porn was just constantly like: ‘I’m here, I’m here, I’m here,’ and so that was when I first noticed it was a problem because I could actively see that I was not being as productive. “Something felt a bit off, but I kind of just pushed that to one side and didn’t really think much of it.” Woodward remembers googling whether porn addiction was even a thing during his teenage years, and found an article which said there might be an issue if someone watched over 10 hours of porn a day. That was way more than Woodward watched on average and justified his continued use. But, as with other addictions, Woodward was taking bigger risks in search of a bigger hit of dopamine. He started swapping content of himself in exchange for videos and pictures of others. Waiting for that message to come in felt exciting, so much so that he’d ignore the possible consequences of his actions. “Looking back now, it was kind of addict behavior really. Not being honest with yourself and justifying things in a strange way to sort of get what you want. But it was never enough,” he said. The painful turning point Then in 2017, the year after he competed at the Olympics, content of Woodward was leaked online. “That was one of the worst moments of my life. It really, really, really crushed me,” he said. “Obviously, it was incredibly embarrassing, and I didn’t know how to deal with that. But it was also just this mirror to myself; what I’d been, what I’d been doing, my actions and how careless I was.” Woodward was still diving competitively at this time and had been trying to stop his porn usage. It was then that he knew something was very wrong. Despite the consequences and how low it made him feel, he couldn’t stop. He realized he was hooked. But acknowledging the problem was the first step to his recovery. As he transitioned away from life as a professional athlete, Woodward joined a cruise company where he would perform diving stunts on ships around the Caribbean. Given everything that had happened, the thought of escaping to a boat was appealing, and it gave him the space to properly discover who he was as a person. Through more reading on the topic and daily meditation, Woodward began tackling his relationship with porn head-on. However, it took him six years of trying before he could finally stop. Now, he’s two years free. Woodward has since decided to speak out about his struggles around a topic that many still find taboo. But the huge response to his story proves that he’s not alone and points to many others suffering with this in silence. Are athletes more vulnerable? Among those who have reached out to him in recent weeks are several athletes, which raises the question as to whether sportspeople are more vulnerable to this addiction than others. And while Woodward agrees that the sample size is too small to find an objective answer to that question, he does believe his profession played a role in developing his addiction – albeit in a convoluted way. Other athletes have spoken out about their similar struggles in the past, including former NFL punter Steve Weatherford, ex-NFL star and current actor Terry Crews and New Zealand Olympian Nick Willis. “I think the kind of people who are likely to become successful athletes are also the kind of people who maybe have a higher probability of having compulsive porn use,” Woodward said, reflecting on his own experience. “You don’t live a normal young life, and I think it’s this high-performance mindset that is a bit of a trap. You pile your self-worth into what you can achieve as an athlete, so if you fail to achieve something good, that means that you have fundamentally failed as a person. I think this expectation, this shame and this blame make porn a crutch that seems more appealing. “It’s the escape, it’s the constant that’s always there for you, that’s not going to challenge you. It’s the thing that’s going to make you feel better in the evening after a bad session. It’s always there. It’s always new.” What the limited research says It’s important to note that porn usage is not yet officially recognized as an addiction. The World Health Organization instead puts it under the umbrella of Compulsive Sexual Behavior Disorder. But research is ongoing into the relatively new issue that seems to have accelerated due to the ease with which people can access porn online. Paula Hall is a sexual and relationship psychotherapist who now looks to help people with excessive porn use through schemes such as the Laurel Centre and Pivotal Recovery. Symptoms of what people call “porn addiction” can differ between individuals, but Hall tells CNN Sports that the bottom line is whether porn is having a detrimental impact on their life – be that in relationships, work or their own self-esteem. Hall refers to it as a spectrum disorder, which mainly impacts men, and where “at the milder end, you’re using pornography for pleasure and, perhaps at that level, it’s completely recreational.” But she added: “What often happens then is it kind of builds and you’re using it as a way to regulate uncomfortable emotions, whether that’s anxiety, depression, loneliness, stress, whatever it might be. “Over time, it goes further to the point where actually you’re using it just to feel normal. So not using it feels difficult.” Hall has worked with several sportspeople regarding their porn use but, like Woodward, is aware there isn’t enough research or evidence to prove any correlation between athletes and porn addiction. But she does recognize that an athlete’s lifestyle, notably during their teenage years, might make them more vulnerable. That’s because budding athletes will tend to avoid other vices such as alcohol, drugs or smoking because it’s detrimental to their game. Porn presents itself as a seemingly harmless way of calming down after the intensity of training and competition. Pro athletes are also on the road a lot, left alone in empty hotel rooms with time on their hands, perhaps unable to form normal romantic relationships because of their hectic timetables. “If you’re a professional sportsperson, there is so much physical control you have to have. You’ve got to watch your diet. Obviously, you’ve got to do your exercise, so there’s a real physical control thing going on,” Hall added. “Porn addiction, and sex addictions, is an opportunity to physiologically release. It’s a place to be out of control in a controlled environment. I think that’s the other reason why it’s popular.” Raising awareness While Hall says there is little research to suggest athletic performance will be severely hampered due to a porn addiction, she doesn’t entirely rule it out. Woodward, who can only reflect on his own lived experience, thinks he did see a drop-off in his sport, both physically but more so mentally. “Let’s say the first time you ever watch porn, you suddenly got this little flick and change in you immediately, and you saw what you would be like and how you would think in 15 years. I think you would be like: ‘Whoa, whoa, okay, I’m not going to touch this,’” he said. “It affected my confidence, it affected my focus, it affected my maturity, it affected my emotional control, it affected my patience. You know, I wonder if it also affected some element of strength.” Now, Woodward has become an ambassador for bringing awareness to an issue that clearly impacts more people than society realizes – or cares to admit. There are still some nights he wakes up wondering whether speaking out was the right decision, but he’s reassured by the messages of support he’s received from people who say listening to his story has made them reassess their relationship with porn. He now wants to help them get the support that he wished he had all those years ago.

articles.title: Jason Kelce’s emotional words about Travis Kelce reveal a deeper side of their famous NFL brotherly rivalry fans rarely see
articles.summary: NFL News: Jason Kelce has made it clear that he has never felt jealous of Travis Kelce’s success. Speaking on Youth Inc. with Greg Olsen, the former Philadelphi.
articles.body: Jason Kelce has made it clear that he has never felt jealous of Travis Kelce’s success. Speaking on Youth Inc. with Greg Olsen, the former Philadelphia Eagles center said he feels proud of what his younger brother has achieved and believes their relationship helped both of them become better people. Jason also pointed to their Super Bowl LVII meeting as proof that even a painful loss could not change how he felt about Travis.Jason Kelce says Travis Kelce’s success never caused resentmentJason Kelce was asked directly about whether Travis Kelce’s success could ever create resentment between the brothers. His answer was simple: no.“I think we’ve both been very successful,” Jason said on Youth Inc. “So, I don’t think that there’s ever been a moment where, like, he can have as much success as he wants in life, and I will be nothing but happy. There’s no resentment because I feel like I’ve maximized what I’ve been given and what I’ve been dealt.”Jason explained that their success has always been connected to the way they pushed each other while growing up. Rather than seeing Travis as someone he needed to beat, he viewed his younger brother as one of the people who helped shape him.“I think that we’ve both become the people, teammates, and men that we are largely due to us, how we challenged each other growing up, how we loved each other, and all of these things have helped make us into the men we are today,” Jason added.That feeling was clear after Super Bowl LVII in 2023. The Eagles lost 38-35 to the Chiefs, giving Travis his second Super Bowl title while Jason walked away without another championship. Still, when the brothers met on the field after the game, Jason hugged Travis and told him to celebrate with his teammates.Jason later became emotional when his mother, Donna Kelce, hugged him. Even then, his focus remained on Travis and the moment his younger brother had just experienced.Travis Kelce and Jason Kelce built success without rivalryJason’s own career gives him plenty to be proud of. He spent all 13 NFL seasons with Philadelphia, earned seven Pro Bowl selections and six first-team All-Pro honors, and helped the Eagles win Super Bowl LII. He retired in March 2024. Reuters also confirmed his retirement after 13 seasons and noted his seven Pro Bowl selections and six first-team All-Pro honors.Travis has built his own impressive career with Kansas City. He returned for his 14th NFL season in 2026 after signing a new one-year deal with the Chiefs. The NFL confirmed that return in March.For Jason, though, the numbers have never been the reason to compare himself with Travis. He believes their relationship made both careers stronger.“Unquestionably, you realize growing up how much stronger you are because of your brother and parents and the people that you’ve allowed close to you in your lives,” Jason said. “And for Trav and I, I don’t think there’s anybody that’s influenced either one of us as people more than each other.”Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Colts Expect WR Keenan Allen to Play in Season Opener and Are Hopeful Alec Pierce Also Returns
articles.summary: INDIANAPOLIS (AP) — The Indianapolis Colts expect receiver Keenan Allen to play in the season opener against the Baltimore Ravens on Sept. 13 despite his recent arrest and remain hopeful injured receiver Alec Pierce is also available.
articles.body:
INDIANAPOLIS (AP) — The Indianapolis Colts expect receiver Keenan Allen to play in the season opener against the Baltimore Ravens on Sept. 13 despite his recent arrest and remain hopeful injured receiver Alec Pierce is also available.

Allen was arrested early Sunday morning on drunken driving charges, and general manager Chris Ballard told reporters Tuesday the team dealt with the incident internally. He did not say specifically what punishment, if any, had been applied.

"He'll play, yes," Ballard said, noting the team does offer players rideshare services. "Fourteen years in the league, no issues, OK? Decorated career, decorated teammate. You know our relationship with Philip Rivers — I know Philip holds him in extremely high regard and (coach) Shane (Steichen) was with him. After you meet his mom and dad, who are amazing people, we feel good about who he is. We unequivocally feel good about who Keenan Allen is."

Allen has not spoken publicly since he was released from custody Sunday afternoon. He is facing preliminary misdemeanor charges of operating a motor vehicle while intoxicated and operating a motor vehicle while intoxicated — endangering a person.

The arrest could lead to a league-imposed suspension though this is the first time in Allen's 14-year pro career he's been cited in a legal matter. He has a court date set for Sept. 16.

Allen was reunited with Steichen when he signed with the Colts on Aug. 18. The 34-year-old Allen is expected to provide a veteran presence as Indy's No. 3 receiver with Pierce and Josh Downs holding the top two spots.

The six-time Pro Bowler played 12 of his first 13 NFL seasons for the Chargers, working with Steichen there for his first seven NFL seasons. In November, Allen surpassed Hall of Famer Antonio Gates as the franchise's career reception leader with No. 956. He spent 2024 with the Chicago Bears before returning to the Chargers last year.

Allen's career total of 1,055 receptions rank 13th on the league's career list, and he begins this season needing 16 catches to pass Colts receivers coach Reggie Wayne for 11th. Among active players, Allen ranks fifth in yards receiving (12,051) and seventh in TD catches (70).

"I'm not going to comment on what happened," Ballard said Tuesday. "But what I am going to tell you is, you know, good people make mistakes and he's a tremendous human being. Give him some grace, and he'll work through the process of the legal system."

He added: "I think over time, he will prove to y'all in this city of who he is, and I think he'll do that in a short amount of time."

Pierce worked out with the team Tuesday after being activated from the physically unable to perform list late last week. He missed all of training camp as he rehabbed from surgery in March for an injured left ankle.

That gives him nearly two weeks to ramp up his activity before the opener.

Will that give him enough time to get into game shape?

"It's good to have him back out there, got a good day of work today," Ballard said. "We'll see going forward, but we're hopeful. We'll see how it ends up landing."

Pierce had platelet-rich plasma injections in January and when that didn't help with the pain, he opted for surgery after signing his four-year, $114 million contract extension.

Last season, Pierce had 47 receptions and 1,003 yards, both career highs, and six touchdowns in 2025. He's led all NFL qualifiers in yards per catch each of the past two seasons.

Steichen is not scheduled to speak with reporters until Thursday, and Ballard deferred to his coach when asked which quarterback, Anthony Richardson or Riley Leonard, would be No. 2 on the depth chart behind incumbent starter Daniel Jones.

The competition remained close throughout camp and the preseason with Richardson and Leonard.

But Ballard insisted Richardson would remain with the Colts, for now, despite his earlier request to be traded. Richardson was the No. 4 overall pick in the 2023 draft and has dealt with a rash of injuries as well as accuracy problems throughout his career.

"We forget how young he is sometimes," Ballard said. "I'm really proud of his growth, really proud of his growth. I thought there was a little bit of a rough start against New England, you know, with the turnovers. But there were two times in camp that I said 'OK, he's really starting to show some poise — the two-minute (drive) against New England and then during the Atlanta scrimmage he had a tremendous two-minute also. So it's been fun to watch Anthony's growth."

articles.title: Packers Express Hope Josh Jacobs, Who Faces Legal Issues, Can Play Sometime This Season
articles.summary: GREEN BAY, Wis. (AP) — Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs still has the support of his coach and general manager, who remain optimistic the three-time Pro Bowler will come off the commissioner's exempt list and play sometime this season.
articles.body:
GREEN BAY, Wis. (AP) — Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs still has the support of his coach and general manager, who remain optimistic the three-time Pro Bowler will come off the commissioner's exempt list and play sometime this season.

Jacobs was placed on the exempt list after being charged with two misdemeanors in a domestic violence case.

"There were many conversations obviously and certainly don't know all the details, but what he tells me, I believe him and I trust him," Packers coach Matt LaFleur said Tuesday. "I'm going to do that until proven otherwise."

General manager Brian Gutekunst said he is hopeful the running back will return before the end of the season. "But we're going to let this process play out, and we'll be prepared either way," Gutekunst said.

Gutekunst said he hasn't seen the video that the Brown County (Wisconsin) District Attorney's office says it has as evidence corroborating statements made by Jacobs' girlfriend regarding their May 23 altercation. Jacobs, who was arrested May 26, faces charges of battery and criminal damage to property.

District Attorney David Lasee announced Thursday that the charges were being filed. Three days later, the NFL put Jacobs on the exempt list, which prevents him from playing or practicing but allows him to keep receiving a paycheck.

Upon request and with the club's permission, Jacobs may be allowed at the facility for meetings, individual workouts, therapy and rehabilitation and other non-football activities.

The NFL is investigating Jacobs' situation and he could be suspended by the league. Any games he misses while on the exempt list would count toward his suspension, but he would also have to repay the money he earned during that time.

LaFleur said the Packers were prepared for the possibility Jacobs might get placed on the list.

"I've seen this guy," LaFleur said. "I've got a love and care and respect for how he is as a person, who he is as a teammate. Obviously a very unfortunate situation, but one that we have to deal with."

Jacobs' lawyers — David Z. Chesnoff, Richard A. Schonfeld, and Clarence F. Duchac III — have noted that the move to the commissioner's exempt list "is not a final determination." They added that Jacobs "looks forward to his return to the team and the NFL."

Hobart-Lawrence police officers who responded to the May 23 call said Jacobs' girlfriend told them she had a lump on her head as a result of Jacobs' actions.

According to police, the woman said she had been looking through Jacobs' phone and saw he was talking to other women, and that she threw the phone in anger without breaking it. She told police that Jacobs had her phone and she told him he could look through it.

According to police, the woman indicated she tried to retrieve her phone from Jacobs, but he grabbed her arm and began a struggle lasting several minutes. They left the home in separate vehicles before eventually returning.

Police said the woman was trying to exit a garage door when Jacobs grabbed her and threw her to the ground, causing her to hit her head. Police said Jacobs also took the phone from her while she was on the ground.

According to the criminal complaint, surveillance footage from the camera system in the garage backed up the woman's statement.

"We have not seen the video," Gutekunst said. "Those are legal things going on right now, so we'll let those play out. ... But in the appropriate times, if those things become available, we'll figure that stuff out when that time comes."

Jacobs' absence hurts Green Bay at a position where it already lacked depth.

MarShawn Lloyd, a third-round draft pick in 2024, has played just one game in two seasons because of injuries, though he's now healthy. Chris Brooks rushed for 106 yards on 27 carries last year.

The Packers acquired 2025 third-round pick Kaleb Johnson from Pittsburgh for a 2028 sixth-round selection on Sunday.

Johnson had 28 carries for 69 yards as a rookie. His second career game was a 31-17 loss at Seattle in which he didn't chase a kickoff that bounced over his head, leading to a Seahawks touchdown.

"I feel like that kickoff killed me, and from then on it was just downhill from there," Johnson said. "I give all respect to the Steelers for giving me a chance and drafting me, but it's 'Go Pack Go' now, so let's go."

Lloyd said he got a lot of assistance from Jacobs, who gave him rides to practice and helped him persevere through his injuries.

Now Lloyd is offering support to his older teammate.

"I don't know what's going on, but that's my brother, so I've just got to stay on that forever," Lloyd said. "He's helped me when I was in the worst part of my life really, those last two years."

The Packers added QB Kedon Slovis to their practice squad. Slovis had been in Arizona's training camp. ... Gutekunst believes WR Savion Williams (ankle) and DE Collin Oliver (Achilles tendon), both on injured reserve, should be ready to return shortly after they've missed the required four games.

articles.title: Jalen Hurts Reacts to AJ Brown's Comments on Relationship After Eagles-Patriots Trade
articles.summary: During an interview with NBC Sports' Maria Taylor on the 7PM in Brooklyn podcast last June, New England Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown admitted that he was not as close as he once was to his old teammate, Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts.
articles.body:
During an interview with NBC Sports' Maria Taylor on the 7PM in Brooklyn podcast last June, New England Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown admitted that he was not as close as he once was to his old teammate, Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts.

Before a joint practice this summer, Brown also let it be known that he hadn't talked to Hurts since being traded, though they ultimately reunited one day later.

On Tuesday, an exclusive interview with Hurts via Zach Baron of GQ Magazine dropped. Baron asked Hurts numerous questions about Brown, including whether he felt the same way as Brown about their relationship, to which the quarterback responded: "Clearly."

The two have been very close in the past. In fact, Hurts is the godfather to Brown's daughter. The two were together on the Eagles from 2022-2025, winning a pair of NFC titles and one Super Bowl.

Brown enjoyed great success on the Eagles, amassing 339 catches, 5,034 receiving yards and 32 touchdowns in four years. He made three All-Pro Second Teams and two Pro Bowls. In addition, Brown accumulated over 1,000 yards in each of his seasons.

Hurts enjoyed great success as well, making three Pro Bowls and even finishing second in the Associated Press NFL MVP race in 2022. The Eagles went 48-15 in his starts, and he accounted for 88 passing touchdowns and 50 rushing scores.

The 2025 season was a bit of a trying year the Eagles at-large, though. Of note, Philadelphia went from seventh in scoring in its 2024 Super Bowl season to 19th in 2025. The Eagles won the NFC East at 11-6 but lost at home to the San Francisco 49ers in the NFC Wild Card round.

By the end of the season and into the offseason, it was clear Brown wanted a fresh start . And so that happened, as Philadelphia traded Brown to the Pats on June 1.

One day later, Brown's interview with Taylor was released. Although Brown said he wasn't as close with Hurts, it's clear he has love and respect for his ex-signal-caller.

"Not as close as we once were," Brown told Taylor (h/t Reuters ). "I believe that's fine. There's no bad blood. There's actually still a lot of love. I love him to death. I ⁠want him to succeed and accomplish all the things that he wants to accomplish.

"I didn't truly understand why our friendship became the center of everyone's attention when it comes to football. Because looking back on it, we haven't been as close as we were for a couple years now. But that didn't stop anything. We still competed, we still pushed each other, we still led the team. It was just kind of strange. People got so fixated on our relationship.

"Im'a say it to you, Im'a say it on camera, I have nothing but love for him. I want him to do well and accomplish everything that his heart desires."

He also made it clear that there wasn't any one incident that led to the two growing apart.

"Nothing happened, people just grow apart," Brown said. "Nothing happened between me and him, or ‌our families, ⁠wives, anything. Nothing like that ever happened. Life happens and you just look up sometimes and you just, you find yourself drifting away and that's fine. And I think both parties accepted that."

As for Hurts, he was asked a few different questions about Brown during the GQ interview. A few of his remarks (and Baron's comments mixed in) can be found below.

"Hurts has a vague answer to my questions about Brown—'You can't replace the greatness that we have achieved and the presence and the success that he's had on the field, but we've got to go to work'—and, when pressed a bit, a slightly more nuanced answer. 'It's a game where we've all got to have a shared mission,' he says, when I ask what happened that things got to the point where Brown reportedly wanted to be traded. 'We all got to be in pursuit of the collective. And it's not something I can speak on from his behalf, but I can tell you my focus has always been to pursue the mission.'

"Unsurprisingly, given the fact that the two men had once been close, much scrutiny had fallen on their relationship. Brown, in the interview he gave after being traded, said the two of them had grown apart. I ask Hurts if he feels the same way. He responds with a single-word answer: 'Clearly.'"

Ultimately, both players are charting new paths.

Brown is the new WR1 in New England, which hopes to build off an impressive AFC Championship-winning season. He'll be working with Drake Maye, the NFL's runner-up to the MVP award.

Hurts is shepherding a new offense led by first-year offensive coordinator (and ex-NFL quarterback) Sean Mannion. DeVonta Smith is the team's new WR1, with first-round draft pick Makai Lemon looking to make an early impact as well.

articles.title: Tony Romo was brutally honest about his arrest and revealed a painful truth about life after football
articles.summary: Tony Romo – a longtime NFL star and the current top analyst on CBS’ NFL broadcasts – pulled back the veil on his post-football life.
articles.body: Athletes can often be perceived as superhuman figures, achieving a kind of elevated status that makes them seem immune to the all-too-human issues that can affect the masses who tune in to watch them compete. On Tuesday, Tony Romo – a longtime NFL star and the current top analyst on CBS’ NFL broadcasts – pulled back that veil. Romo was arrested last month on suspicion of operating a vehicle while intoxicated in Wisconsin, a moment that stained his image as the aw-shucks, clean-cut football star who has become one of the best on-air personalities in the game. In a statement where he announced he had pleaded no contest to a civil offense for operating while intoxicated, Romo gave a stark look at what life is like after a player leaves the game. “Multiple back surgeries ended my career earlier than I expected and left me with constant, debilitating pain. That pain led to a dependence on pain medication, and my efforts to get off those medications led to an over-reliance on alcohol,” Romo wrote in his statement. That statement gave voice to a story that’s often suffered in silence by former professional athletes: Their playing days left them with pain that sticks around long after the fans have stopped cheering. When few are watching, those athletes face a reckoning over the physical sacrifices they made to chase their dreams. And, as Romo notes, dealing with those sacrifices in the years after leaving the gridiron can sometimes lead to destructive choices – such as an over-reliance on substances that mask the pain. But the lessons taught by sports can also provide a path back – at least, that’s what Romo believes. In his statement, he said football taught him “the power of relationships, the strength of a team and the toughness to face failure head-on with honesty, resilience and the determination to do better.” He believes those qualities will help him carve out the next steps in his post-career life. “As I have taught my three young sons: when you fall short, you stand up and take full responsibility. That is an important first step. The harder and more important step is examining the path that brought you here and making the changes necessary to move forward,” he wrote. “That path requires honesty. None of this is an excuse. These are my failures, and I take responsibility for them.” The incredible highs of athletic success can sometimes be matched by the lows that follow a professional playing career and Romo is far from alone in having to pick up the pieces after an arrest. Tiger Woods is due back in court on Wednesday for his criminal case relating to an arrest earlier this year after a car crash. Police accused Woods of being inebriated and found prescription painkillers in his pocket. Woods sought treatment after the arrest and went to Switzerland for weeks. Woods is another prominent athlete whose career left him dealing with chronic pain. The violent swings that powered his game, launching golf balls far beyond his competitors, also wrecked his back and knees. Woods has been involved in multiple car crashes and each time prescription painkillers have been linked to the incidents. Golf and football can hardly be more different as athletic contests. And yet, both Woods and Romo faced similar challenges as their athletic primes faded away – chronic pain and the struggle to deal with it, often leading to substance use. Romo said he’s now trying to find a way forward, working with a medical team to address how he can better cope with the pain as he moves toward a return to the airwaves. “The past month has been difficult, but it has also been personally significant. It has required me to confront and own my mistakes fully—to the Lord, to myself, to my family, and now to the public,” he wrote. “I am working closely with a team of doctors to address my health and make the necessary changes. I am deeply grateful for the support of my family, my friends, and the NFL community including players, coaches, and owners. Your encouragement has meant more to me than you know.”

articles.title: CeeDee Lamb Post Video of Utah Retreat With Cowboys' Dak Prescott, George Pickens, More
articles.summary: CeeDee Lamb provided a closer look at a recent Utah retreat that he went on with Dallas Cowboys teammates, including Dak Prescott and George Pickens in a video posted to his YouTube channel on Tuesday.
articles.body:
CeeDee Lamb provided a closer look at a recent Utah retreat that he went on with Dallas Cowboys teammates, including Dak Prescott and George Pickens in a video posted to his YouTube channel on Tuesday.

"Three days away with the guys to reset, compete, and spend time with each other before the season gets going," Lamb wrote in the caption of the video. "Golf, workout, hoops, a few drinks, and a whole lot of competition in between. Nothing serious, just some good energy, and time away from ball with the fellas."

Prescott has made it an annual tradition to take Dallas' skill position players on a retreat before the beginning of training camp.

The Cowboys are looking to remain explosive offensively in 2026 after ranking No. 2 among all teams by averaging 391.9 total yards per game last season.

Prescott threw for 4,552 yards and 30 touchdowns compared to 10 interceptions while Pickens wrapped up a breakout year in which he amassed a career-high 1,429 receiving yards and nine touchdowns.

Although Lamb was limited to 14 games, he still caught 75 passes for 1,077 yards.

Dallas ultimately missed the playoffs with a 7-9-1 record, as it owned the worst scoring defense in the NFL after allowing 30.1 points per game.

The Cowboys will hope to take a step forward defensively following an offseason in which they traded for pass-rusher Rashan Gary and signed safety Jalen Thompson. Dallas added former Ohio State safety Caleb Downs with the No. 11 overall pick in the 2026 NFL draft as well.

The Cowboys will open their 2026 campaign against the New York Giants on Sept. 13.
